facts.fact: The Quito Metropolitan Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Quito, Ecuador.
facts.quote: The Quito Metropolitan Cathedral (Spanish: Catedral Metropolitana de Quito), is a Catholic cathedral in Quito, Ecuador.

facts.fact: It stands on the southwestern side of the Plaza de la Independencia (Plaza Grande) and was the seat of the Diocese of Quito from 1545 until 1848, when it became an archdiocese.
facts.quote: Located on the southwestern side of the Plaza de la Independencia (La Plaza Grande), it (and its predecessor building) served as a seat of the Diocese of Quito from 1545 until 1848 when it was elevated to Archdiocese.

facts.fact: It was built of stone using the minga system, a local tradition of communal hauling, carving and masonry.
facts.quote: Construction was of stone and the minga system (a local traditional practice of communal hauling, carving, and masonry) was utilized.

facts.fact: Its main entrance does not face the Plaza because a deep gorge at the time of construction stopped the building from extending backwards.
facts.quote: The anomaly of the main entrance not fronting onto the Plaza is explained by the presence of a deep gorge (la quebrada de Sanguña or Zanguña) present at the time of construction, which precluded extending the building backwards (toward the southwest).

facts.fact: In 1797–1799 the Spanish military engineer Antonio García added the Carondelet Arch.
facts.quote: The cathedral was enhanced in 1797–1799, during the administration of the 20th President of the Real Audiencia Baron Héctor de Carondelet, by the addition of the Carondelet Arch, a work of Spanish military engineer Antonio García.

facts.fact: Its plan of three naves with semi-ogival arches on square pillars is typical of the 16th century, and some experts call its style Gothic-Mudéjar.
facts.quote: Built on a plan comprising three longitudinal naves surmounted by semi-ogival arches on square pillars, the basic spatial structure of the cathedral is typical of the 16th century. Based upon interior features — especially the details of the pillars, arches, and the carved and coffered ceiling — some experts assert that the cathedral should be characterized as Gothic-Mudéjar in style.

facts.fact: Three domes clad in glazed green ceramic rise over the transept, the high altar and the Carondelet Arch.
facts.quote: Three attractive domes dressed in glazed green ceramic rise atop the transept, the high altar, and the Carondelet Arch.

facts.fact: After a 1987 earthquake the city restored the cathedral's deep foundations using micropile technology.
facts.quote: In the wake of a 1987 earthquake, the municipality of Quito has structurally restored the deep foundations of the cathedral with micropile technology.

facts.fact: The Casa de Nariño is the official residence and main workplace of the President of Colombia.
facts.quote: The Casa de Nariño (Spanish pronunciation: ['kasa ðe na'riɲo]), literally the House of Nariño, is the official residence and principal workplace of the President of Colombia.

facts.fact: It was dedicated in 1908, built on the site of the house where Antonio Nariño was born.
facts.quote: It was dedicated in 1908 after being constructed on the site of the house where Antonio Nariño was born.

facts.fact: It was designed by Gastón Lelarge, a French-born former pupil of Charles Garnier, with Julián Lombana.
facts.quote: The design was made by architects Gastón Lelarge, a French-born former pupil of Charles Garnier, and Julián Lombana.

facts.fact: The architects extended the property to Eighth Road, reorganised the inside on two levels, designed wide halls and improved the façade with carved stone.
facts.quote: The architects extended the dimensions of the property to Eighth Road and restructured the inner part of the building by creating two levels. They also designed wide halls and improved the façade with carved stones.

facts.fact: All the ornamentation was carried out by the Swiss sculptor Luigi Ramelli.
facts.quote: The complete ornamentation works were carried out by the Swiss sculptor Luigi Ramelli.

facts.fact: The building was rededicated in 1980 after additions were built.
facts.quote: In 1980, the structure was rededicated after the construction of additions.

facts.fact: The restoration works were carried out by the architect Fernando Alsina.
facts.quote: The restoration works were carried out by the architect Fernando Alsina, who was an auditor of the Ministry of public works.

facts.fact: Its garden holds the Bogotá Astronomical Observatory, designed by the Capuchin friar-architect Domingo de Petrés and built in 1802–03.
facts.quote: Its garden houses the Observatorio Astronómico de Bogotá, designed by the Capuchin friar-architect Domingo de Petrés and built in 1802–03.

facts.fact: Bharat Mandapam is an exhibition hall in the Pragati Maidan complex in New Delhi, India.
facts.quote: Bharat Mandapam (English: /ˈbʱaːrət̪ ˈməɳɖəpəm/) is an exhibition hall located within the confines of the Pragati Maidan complex in New Delhi, India.

facts.fact: It was unveiled in 2023, ahead of the G20 summit held in New Delhi that year.
facts.quote: While the Pragati Maidan complex was inaugurated in 1972, Bharat Mandapam was unveiled in 2023 ahead of the 2023 G20 New Delhi summit.

facts.fact: It was built on the site of the Hall of Nations, which was controversially demolished in 2017 while court proceedings on its heritage status were still underway.
facts.quote: It was constructed on the site of the Hall of Nations, which was controversially razed in 2017 despite court proceedings underway to address the structure’s heritage status.

facts.fact: The demolished Hall of Nations, by Raj Rewal, had been celebrated as the world's first and then largest space-frame structure in reinforced concrete.
facts.quote: Designed by architect Raj Rewal, the Hall was celebrated as the world’s first and then-largest space-frame structure built in reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: In 2016 a consortium of Arcop (Delhi) and Aedas (Singapore), led by Sanjay Singh and Simón Núñez de Arenas Fraile, won the competition for the master plan and the design of the exhibition halls and convention centre.
facts.quote: In 2016, a consortium of architecture firms, Arcop (Delhi) and Aedas (Singapore), led by architects Sanjay Singh and Spaniard Simón Núñez de Arenas Fraile respectively, won the competition for the Master Plan and architectural design of the exhibition halls and the convention center.

facts.fact: The complex has a built-up area of 390,000 square metres, a meeting hall for 7,000 people and six exhibition halls with 150,000 square metres of exhibition space.
facts.quote: With a total built-up area of 390,000 sq. metres, the complex includes a meeting hall that can accommodate 7,000 people in a single format, along with six modern exhibition halls spanning an exhibition area of 150,000 sq. metres.

facts.fact: The centre cost more than ₹2,600 crore and was built by the National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC).
facts.quote: The Integrated Exhibition-cum-Convention Centre (IECC) at Pragati Maidan, developed at a cost exceeding ₹2,600 crore, was constructed by the National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC).

facts.fact: Yashobhoomi is a convention centre in Sector 25, Dwarka, Delhi, India.
facts.quote: Yashobhoomi is a convention center located in Sector 25, Dwarka, Delhi, India.

facts.fact: It is the largest convention centre in India and Asia by area.
facts.quote: It is the largest convention center in India and Asia by area, and one of the biggest MICE facilities in the world.

facts.fact: Its first phase was inaugurated on 17 September 2023.
facts.quote: The first phase of Yashobhoomi was inaugurated on 17 September 2023.

facts.fact: It has 15 convention halls, including the main auditorium, the Grand Ballroom and 13 meeting rooms, holding 11,000 people in all.
facts.quote: It has 15 convention centres, which include the main auditorium, the Grand Ballroom and 13 meeting centres, having a total capacity of holding 11,000 people.

facts.fact: The main auditorium's decoration draws on Indian culture: terrazzo floors with brass inlays in rangoli patterns, hanging sound-absorbing metal cylinders and lit patterned walls.
facts.quote: The main auditorium has many features for decoration inspired from Indian culture, such as terrazzo floors with brass inlays representing rangoli patterns, suspended sound absorbent metal cylinders and lit-up patterned walls.

facts.fact: Automated seating lets the auditorium floor switch between a flat floor and tiered seating.
facts.quote: The auditorium has many innovative automated seating systems, one of which allows the floor to be a flat floor or an auditorium style tiered seating for different seating configurations.

facts.fact: The Grand Ballroom has a petal-themed ceiling.
facts.quote: The Grand Ballroom has a petal-themed design on the ceiling and has interior as well as exterior seating areas.

facts.fact: The complex reuses all its wastewater, harvests rainwater and has rooftop solar panels on all its buildings.
facts.quote: The complex is equipped with an advanced wastewater treatment plant with 100 percent wastewater reusing and rainwater harvesting systems for water construction and rooftop solar panels on all structures for clean and sustainable energy and electricity generation.

facts.fact: It has received the Indian Green Building Council's "Green Cities Platinum" certification.
facts.quote: Because of these eco-friendly measures, the complex has received "Green Cities Platinum" certification from Indian Green Building Council (IGBC).

facts.fact: Christ Church (Christuskirche) is a historic Lutheran church and landmark in Windhoek, Namibia.
facts.quote: The Christ Church (German: Christuskirche) is a historic landmark and Lutheran church in Windhoek, Namibia, belonging to the German-speaking Evangelical Lutheran Church in Namibia.

facts.fact: It was designed by the architect Gottlieb Redecker.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect Gottlieb Redecker.

facts.fact: It was built as a symbol of peace after the wars between the Germans and the Herero and Nama.
facts.quote: The church was built as a symbol of peace following the wars between the Germans, and the Herero and Nama.

facts.fact: The foundation stone was laid on 11 August 1907 and the church was dedicated on 16 October 1910.
facts.quote: The foundation stone was laid on 11 August 1907, while on 16 October 1910 the church was officially dedicated.

facts.fact: It is built of quartz sandstone quarried near the Avis Dam.
facts.quote: The Christ Church was constructed from quartz sandstone mined from the vicinity of the Avis Dam.

facts.fact: Its architecture mixes neo-Romanesque, Art Nouveau and Gothic Revival influences.
facts.quote: The architecture displays a mixture of neo-Romanesque, Art Nouveau and Gothic Revival influences.

facts.fact: Its spire is 24 m high, and the portico is made of Carrara marble imported from Italy.
facts.quote: Its spire is 24 m (79 ft) high. The portico was made from Carrara marble imported from Italy.

facts.fact: The coloured stained-glass windows in the sanctuary were a gift from Emperor Wilhelm II.
facts.quote: The colorful stained lead glass windows in the sanctuary were a gift from Emperor Wilhelm II.

facts.fact: The Acropolium, also called Saint Louis Cathedral, is a former Catholic church in Carthage, Tunisia.
facts.quote: The Acropolium, also known as Saint Louis Cathedral (French: Cathédrale Saint-Louis de Carthage), is a former Latin Catholic church located in Carthage, Tunisia.

facts.fact: It sits on the top of Byrsa Hill near the ruins of the Punic and Roman city, built over the ruins of a temple to Eshmun, the Punic god of healing.
facts.quote: The cathedral sits on the peak of Byrsa Hill, near the ruins of the ancient Punic and then Roman city. It was built atop the ruins of an old temple dedicated to Eshmun, the Punic god of healing.

facts.fact: It was built between 1884 and 1890, under the French protectorate.
facts.quote: Built between 1884 and 1890, under the French protectorate, the cathedral acquired primacy for all of Africa when the title of primate of Africa was restored for the benefit of Cardinal Lavigerie, titular of the Archdioceses of Algiers and of Carthage, united in his person.

facts.fact: Cardinal Lavigerie dedicated it to Saint Louis, who died near the spot during the Eighth Crusade in 1270.
facts.quote: Cardinal Lavigerie dedicated the church to Saint Louis, who died on that approximate spot during the Eighth Crusade in 1270.

facts.fact: Built to the plans of the abbot Pougnet, it draws on Byzantine, Gothic and Moorish styles and has a Latin-cross plan of 65 by 30 metres.
facts.quote: The building, constructed according to the plans of the abbot Pougnet, is inspired by Byzantine, Gothic, and Moorish architectural style, and is in the shape of a Latin cross of 65 meters by 30.

facts.fact: Two square towers frame the façade, and a large cupola ringed by eight short towers rises over the crossing, with a smaller cupola above the apse.
facts.quote: The façade is framed by two square towers, the crossing lies beneath a large cupola surrounded by eight short towers or spires, and there is a smaller cupola above the apse.

facts.fact: The church has 284 stained-glass windows.
facts.quote: The church has 284 stained glass windows.

facts.fact: It is no longer used for worship and now hosts public events and concerts.
facts.quote: It is no longer used for worship, but instead hosts public events or concerts of Tunisian music and classical music.

facts.fact: The Bourguiba Mausoleum in Monastir, Tunisia, is the monumental grave of Habib Bourguiba, the father of Tunisian independence.
facts.quote: The Bourguiba mausoleum (Arabic: ضريح بورقيبة, romanized: Ḍarīḥ Būrqībah) is a monumental grave in Monastir, Tunisia, containing the remains of former president Habib Bourguiba, the father of Tunisian independence, who died on April 6, 2000.

facts.fact: It was built in 1963, while Bourguiba was still alive, in a modern Arab-Muslim style.
facts.quote: The mausoleum was built while Bourguiba was still alive, in 1963, in the modern Arab-Muslim style.

facts.fact: It stands in the western part of the Sidi El Mézeri cemetery, at the end of a main alley about 200 m long and 30 m wide.
facts.quote: It is located in the western part of the Sidi El Mézeri cemetery, the main burial site in the city, at the end of the main alley which is about 200 m (660 ft) long and 30 m (98 ft) wide.

facts.fact: Two 25-metre minarets flank the building, which is topped by a golden dome between two green domes.
facts.quote: The building is flanked by two 25-metre-high (82 ft) minarets and topped by a golden dome between two green domes.

facts.fact: Its entrance gate and the gate separating it from the cemetery are examples of Tunisian art.
facts.quote: The mausoleum entrance gate and the gate that separates it from the rest of the cemetery are examples of Tunisian art.

facts.fact: It was expanded in 1978.
facts.quote: It was expanded in 1978.

facts.fact: Inside is a small museum of Bourguiba's belongings, including his desk from the Carthage presidential palace.
facts.quote: Inside the mausoleum, there is a small museum housing some of president Bourguiba's personal belongings: his desk from the presidential palace of Carthage, his pens, passports and identity card, his glasses, and also his photos and his clothes (both Western and traditional: jebba, chéchia, and fez).

facts.fact: The Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque is a mosque, mausoleum and Sufi shrine in the Anfoushi neighbourhood of Alexandria, Egypt.
facts.quote: The Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque (Arabic: جامع أبو العباس المرسي, romanized: Jami' Abu al-'Abbas al-Mursi) is a mosque, mausoleum, and Sufi shrine, located in the Anfoushi neighbourhood of Alexandria, on the north coast of Egypt.

facts.fact: It honours Abu'l Abbas al-Mursi, a 13th-century mystic who is buried there.
facts.quote: The 13th-century mosque is named in honour of Abu'l Abbas al-Mursi, a 13th-century mystic, who is also buried in the same place along with members of the Ashraf family.

facts.fact: In 1934 King Fouad I ordered a 3,200-square-metre courtyard (sahn) that brought together three mosque-shrines, with this mosque in the middle.
facts.quote: In 1934, King Fouad I ordered the construction of a 3,200-square-metre (34,000 sq ft) sahn, to include the mosque-shrines of the Al-Busiri and Yaqut al-Arshy, with the mosque of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mursi standing in the middle.

facts.fact: The Italian architect Mario Rossi planned the design and decoration, and construction took sixteen or eighteen years.
facts.quote: Mario Rossi, an Italian architect, was involved in planning the design and decor of the mosque, and construction took sixteen or eighteen years.

facts.fact: The present mosque, especially its exterior, is in a Neo-Mamluk style inspired by late Mamluk architecture.
facts.quote: The current mosque, particularly its exterior, is designed in a Neo-Mamluk style, inspired by late Mamluk architecture in particular.

facts.fact: Its pillars are granite, four of them of a harder granite made in Italy to carry the heavy dome.
facts.quote: The pillars of the mosque are made of granite, with four of them being made from harder granite that was designed in Italy to support the heavy dome.

facts.fact: A large dome and four smaller domes, standing for the saint and his disciples, top the mosque, and its minaret is about 73 metres high.
facts.quote: A large dome tops the mosque, followed by four smaller domes meant to represent the saint and his disciples. The mosque's minaret is approximately 73 metres (240 ft) high.

facts.fact: The finished mosque was a source of inspiration for the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi.
facts.quote: The final structure of the mosque served as a source of inspiration for the much larger Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi, which was finally completed in 2007 after more than a decade of building work.

facts.fact: Cape Town Stadium is a football and rugby stadium in Cape Town, South Africa, built for the 2010 FIFA World Cup.
facts.quote: The Cape Town Stadium (Afrikaans: Kaapstad-stadion; Xhosa: Inkundla yezemidlalo yaseKapa; known since 2021 as the DHL Stadium for sponsorship reasons) is a football (soccer) and rugby union stadium in Cape Town, South Africa, that was built as part of the country's hosting of the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

facts.fact: It stands in Green Point, between Signal Hill and the Atlantic Ocean, close to the city centre and the V&A Waterfront.
facts.quote: The stadium is located in Green Point, between Signal Hill and the Atlantic Ocean, close to the Cape Town city center and to the Victoria & Alfred Waterfront, a popular tourist and shopping venue.

facts.fact: Construction began in March 2007 on the Green Point Common.
facts.quote: Construction of the Cape Town Stadium, located on the Green Point Common, began in March 2007.

facts.fact: Contractors Murray & Roberts and WBHO finished it in 33 months, at a cost of R4.4 billion (about US$600 million).
facts.quote: In 33 months, joint venture contractors Murray & Roberts, now known as Concor and WBHO completed the project at a cost of R4.4billion – or approximately US$600million.

facts.fact: The architects were GMP Architects of Germany with the local firms Louis Karol Architects and Point Architects.
facts.quote: The project architects were an association between GMP Architects of Germany and local firms, Louis Karol Architects and the joint venture practice Point Architects comprising Comrie Wilkinson Architects and Urban Designers, Jakupa Architects and Urban Designers, Munnik Visser Architects and Paragon Architects.

facts.fact: It seated 64,100 during the 2010 World Cup, later reduced to 55,000.
facts.quote: The stadium had a seating capacity of 64,100 during the 2010 World Cup, later reduced to 55,000.

facts.fact: After the World Cup, temporary seats on the top tier were replaced with event suites and clubrooms.
facts.quote: Following the World Cup, temporary rows of seating on either side on the top tier were replaced by events suites and clubrooms, reducing the stadium's capacity to 55,000.

facts.fact: Green Point Park around the stadium was completed within a year of the World Cup, as promised during public consultation.
facts.quote: The Greenpoint Park was completed within a year of the World Cup ending as was promised to the people of Cape Town during the public consultation process preceding stadium construction.

facts.fact: Durban City Hall is a historic city hall in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
facts.quote: Durban City Hall is a historic city hall located at Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

facts.fact: It was designed by Stanley G. Hudson and built between 1906 and 1910.
facts.quote: The building was designed by architect Stanley G. Hudson and erected between 1906 and 1910.

facts.fact: It is in an Edwardian neobaroque style and is almost an exact replica of Belfast City Hall.
facts.quote: The building, which features an Edwardian neobaroque style, is almost an exact replica of Belfast City Hall in Northern Ireland.

facts.fact: Its façades carry allegorical statues of the arts, music, literature, commerce and industry.
facts.quote: The façades are decorated by allegorical statues depicting the arts, music, literature, commerce and industry.

facts.fact: The Capital Museum is a public municipal art museum in Beijing, China.
facts.quote: The Capital Museum (Chinese: 首都博物馆) is a public municipal art museum in Beijing, China.

facts.fact: It opened in 1981 and moved into its present building in 2006.
facts.quote: It opened in 1981 and moved into its present building in 2006

facts.fact: The museum's massive roof and the sloping entrance square are the work of the architects Jean-Marie Duthilleul and Cui Kai.
facts.quote: The Capital Museum's massive roof and the gradient at the entrance square is the work of architects Jean-Marie Duthilleul and Cui Kai.

facts.fact: The design draws on ancient Chinese architecture, and its stone outer wall was meant to symbolise the city walls and towers of ancient China.
facts.quote: It was influenced by ancient Chinese architecture, and the stone-made exterior wall was meant to symbolize the city walls and towers of ancient China.

facts.fact: A danbi, a massive stone carved with dragons, phoenixes and imperial objects, is set into the ground in front of the north gate.
facts.quote: A piece of danbi (a massive stone carved with images of dragon, phoenix and imperial artifacts) is embedded on the ground in front of the north gate of the museum.

facts.fact: A Ming dynasty decorative archway in the reception hall shows the 'central axis' common in Chinese architecture.
facts.quote: A decorative archway from the Ming Dynasty, set in the reception hall, shows the "central axis" feature that is commonly seen in Chinese architecture.

facts.fact: The oval Bronze Exhibition Hall slants from the ground out through the museum's exterior, meant to symbolise the unearthing of ancient relics.
facts.quote: The Bronze Exhibition Hall, which has an oval-shape, was meant to symbolize the unearthing of ancient relics by its slanting design which extends from the ground to the exterior of the museum.

facts.fact: The Digital Beijing Building is a 57-metre block-shaped building put up as a data centre for the 2008 Summer Olympics.
facts.quote: It is a 57-metre-tall (187 ft) block-shaped building erected to serve as a data center during the 2008 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: It was the only major facility on Olympic Green that was not an event venue, and the only major Olympic facility designed by a Chinese architect.
facts.quote: It was the only major facility on Olympic Green not to be an event venue for the games, and the only major Olympic facility designed by a Chinese architect.

facts.fact: Its architect, Pei Zhu, was interested in links between traditional Chinese design and digital technology; the building looks like a circuit board from the sides and a bar code from the ends.
facts.quote: That architect, Pei Zhu, was interested in the connections between traditional Chinese design and digital technology. He produced a sustainable building that resembles a circuit board when viewed from either side and a bar code when viewed from either end, in the process using some new materials for the first time in China.

facts.fact: It is made of four tall, narrow slabs, 11 storeys (57 m) high and of different thicknesses, with gaps between them.
facts.quote: It consists of four large narrow slabs 11 stories (57 metres (187 ft)) high but of varying thickness, with the easternmost thickest of all, with gaps between them, with the gap between the eastern slab and the others being wider.

facts.fact: The slabs are faced in a dark stone quarried in northern China, with some aluminium inserts made to look like stone.
facts.quote: They are faced in a dark stone quarried in northern China, with some inserts of aluminum made to look like stone.

facts.fact: At night green LEDs blink in a descending pattern down the east façade.
facts.quote: At night a series of green LEDs blink in a descending fashion down the 1,323-square-metre (14,240 sq ft) east facade.

facts.fact: Inside, the floors are a translucent fibre-reinforced plastic, first developed as a substitute for jade, which takes projected images as a 'digital carpet'.
facts.quote: The first, a translucent fiber reinforced plastic, had first been developed for a hotel Zhu was building elsewhere in Beijing as a substitute for jade, which proved too expensive to use in the quantity he had wanted it. Since it held images projected in it well, he also decided to use it for the flooring inside Digital Beijing, where it could become a "digital carpet", similar to the "urban carpet" Zaha Hadid created for the Rosenthal Center for Contemporary Art in Cincinnati, Ohio.

facts.fact: The building was completed and opened on 3 November 2007.
facts.quote: The building was completed and opened on 3 November 2007.

facts.fact: It was shortlisted in its category at the 2008 World Architecture Festival.
facts.quote: Two months after the Olympics, at that year's World Architecture Festival, Digital Beijing was shortlisted in its category.

facts.fact: The Presidential Office Building is the official workplace of the president of the Republic of China on Taiwan.
facts.quote: The Presidential Office Building is the official workplace of the president of the Republic of China on Taiwan.

facts.fact: Designed by Uheiji Nagano during Japanese rule, it was built to house the Office of the Governor-General of Taiwan.
facts.quote: The building, located in the Zhongzheng District in the national capital — Taipei, was designed by architect Uheiji Nagano during the period of Japanese rule of Taiwan (1895–1945). The structure originally housed the Office of the Governor-General of Taiwan.

facts.fact: Its design shows traits typical of Japanese architects in colonial Taiwan: an east-facing façade and a blend of Renaissance, Baroque and neoclassical elements.
facts.quote: Aspects of the design typical of Japanese architects in Taiwan's colonial period include a façade facing east and a creative blend of traditional European elements (Renaissance, Baroque and neoclassical).

facts.fact: Authorities in Tokyo raised the planned central tower from six storeys to 11.
facts.quote: Tokyo authorities increased the height of the initial six-story central tower to 11 stories and made defensive improvements to the defense and corner towers.

facts.fact: It was built between 1 June 1912 and 31 March 1919 at a cost of 2.8 million yen.
facts.quote: Construction began on 1 June 1912 and was completed on 31 March 1919 at a cost of 2.8 million Japanese yen.

facts.fact: Its 130-metre façade faces east down Ketagalan Boulevard, reflecting the Japanese practice of facing important buildings toward the rising sun at the head of long avenues.
facts.quote: The 130 meter-wide facade faces east down multi-lane Ketagalan Boulevard. This reflects the concerns of its Japanese architects, who often oriented important structures toward the rising sun at the head of long avenues.

facts.fact: Its 60-metre central tower was the tallest structure in the Taipei Basin during Japanese rule.
facts.quote: The 60-meter tower at the center of the building was the tallest structure in the Taipei Basin during Japanese rule.

facts.fact: After heavy bombing in 1945, a restoration involving about 81,000 workers was completed at the end of 1948.
facts.quote: The restoration involved approximately 81,000 workers and was completed at the end of 1948, looking only slightly different from the original building.

facts.fact: It was declared a historic national monument in 1998.
facts.quote: 1998: the building is declared a historic national monument by Ministry of the Interior.

facts.fact: Bug Dome was a bamboo shelter built for the 2009 Shenzhen and Hong Kong Bi-City Biennale of Urbanism/Architecture by a group of architects calling themselves WEAK!
facts.quote: Bug Dome was a bamboo shelter created for the Shenzhen & Hong Kong bi-city Biennale of Urbanism/Architecture in Shenzhen 2009, China by a group of architects calling themselves WEAK!

facts.fact: It was inspired by the homes built by insects.
facts.quote: The Bug Dome was inspired by the homes built by insects.

facts.fact: It was designed as a sheltered space for underground band performances, poetry readings and discussions during the Biennale.
facts.quote: It was designed to be a sheltered area where underground band performances, poetry readings, and discussions could take place during the SZHK Biennale.

facts.fact: WEAK! was a collaboration of Hsieh Ying-Chun, Roan Ching-Yueh and the Finnish architect Marco Casagrande.
facts.quote: WEAK! was a collaboration of Hsieh Ying-Chun, a Taiwan architectural activist specializing at collaborative construction and sustainable construction, Roan Ching-Yueh, an architect, curator and art critic, and Marco Casagrande, a Finnish architect, founder of C-lab.

facts.fact: It was built of bamboo and 'weak concrete', cement mixed with soil.
facts.quote: The 'bug dome' was constructed out of bamboo and weak concrete in the form of cement mixed with soil.

facts.fact: All its materials were gathered from around the site and are meant to return to nature when the dome is no longer needed.
facts.quote: All the necessary materials were collected from around the building site and will return to the natural environment when the Dome is no longer needed.

facts.fact: After the Biennale, it became a gathering place for migrant workers living in nearby shelters and abandoned buildings.
facts.quote: After the Biennale, the shelter continued to be used as gathering place for illegal workers from the Chinese countryside, many of whom were living in nearby shelters and abandoned buildings.

facts.fact: The Yuz Museum is a museum in the West Bund, Xuhui District, Shanghai, run by the non-profit Yuz Foundation.
facts.quote: The Yuz Museum Shanghai (Chinese: 余德耀美术馆) is a museum in the West Bund in Xuhui District, Shanghai, China, operated by the non-profit Yuz Foundation.

facts.fact: Designed by Sou Fujimoto, it occupies the renovated hangar of the former Shanghai Longhua Airport, with more than 9,000 square metres including a main gallery of over 3,000 square metres.
facts.quote: Designed by Japanese architect Sou Fujimoto, it is located in the renovated hangar of the former Shanghai Longhua Airport, occupying premises with a total area of more than 9,000 square meters, including a main gallery of over 3,000 square meters.

facts.fact: It opened on 17 May 2014.
facts.quote: The museum opened on 17 May 2014.

facts.fact: It was founded by the Chinese-Indonesian collector Budi Tek.
facts.quote: The Yuz Museum was founded by Budi Tek, a Chinese-Indonesian entrepreneur, philanthropist, and art collector.

facts.fact: The hangar-converted great hall holds large art installations, while the other galleries give more than 1,000 square metres to paintings, sculpture and photography.
facts.quote: Designed by Japanese architect Sou Fujimoto and built on the old site of the aircraft hangar of the former Long Hua Airport, the museum boasts a total area of 9,000 square meters, among which the hangar-converted great hall alone covers over 3,000 square meters, complementing the numerous large-scale art installations, while the other galleries offer more than 1,000 square meters for paintings, sculptures and photography of contemporary art.

facts.fact: Chengdu Museum is a public municipal museum in Chengdu, Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: Chengdu Museum (Chinese: 成都博物馆) is a public municipal museum in Chengdu, Sichuan, China.

facts.fact: It stands on the west side of Tianfu Square, near the Sichuan Art Museum and the Sichuan Provincial Library.
facts.quote: The museum is located on the west side of Tianfu Square, close to the Jincheng Art Palace, Sichuan Art Museum, Sichuan Provincial Library, and Sichuan Science and Technology Museum.

facts.fact: In 2007 Sutherland Hussey Harris, with the Beijing firm Pansolution, won first prize in an international competition to design the new city museum.
facts.quote: In 2007, the architects Sutherland Hussey Harris, together with Pansolution, based in Beijing, won the first prize in an international competition to design a new city museum for Chengdu.

facts.fact: The building was completed in 2016 with a floor area of 65,000 square metres.
facts.quote: The museum building was completed in 2016 with a floor area of 65,000 m2 and named Chengdu Museum New Hall.

facts.fact: It has six floors of exhibits.
facts.quote: The museum has six floors displaying historic artifacts.

facts.fact: It is Chengdu's largest comprehensive museum, with nearly 200,000 objects from the Neolithic to the Republic of China.
facts.quote: The museum is the largest comprehensive museum in Chengdu with nearly 200,000 objects in its collections, covering a time period from the Neolithic period to that of the Republic of China.

facts.fact: The Auditorium Building is a mixed-use early skyscraper on South Michigan Avenue in the Loop, Chicago.
facts.quote: The Auditorium Building is a mixed-use early skyscraper at 430 South Michigan Avenue in the Loop community area of Chicago, Illinois, United States.

facts.fact: It was built between 1887 and 1889 to the design of Adler & Sullivan, the partnership of Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler.
facts.quote: Built between 1887 and 1889, it was designed by Adler & Sullivan, the partnership of Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler.

facts.fact: It first held the Auditorium Theatre, offices and a hotel; the theatre survives, and the rest is now classrooms for Roosevelt University.
facts.quote: It originally included the Auditorium Theatre, offices, and a hotel; the theater still exists, but the rest of the building has since been converted into classrooms for Roosevelt University.

facts.fact: It is mostly 10 storeys high, with a 17-storey, 73-metre tower on the south.
facts.quote: The building is generally 10 stories high, except for a 17-story, 240-foot-tall (73 m) tower to the south.

facts.fact: The façade is darker granite and lighter limestone, divided into three horizontal sections.
facts.quote: The facade is generally made of darker granite and lighter limestone and is divided into three horizontal sections.

facts.fact: Its structure rests on grillage and pyramidal footings and has an iron and steel frame.
facts.quote: Its structural design includes a foundation of grillages and pyramidal footings, along with an iron and steel superstructure.

facts.fact: The theatre takes up 40% of the building's volume and seats 4,200 on three levels.
facts.quote: Inside, the theater occupies 40% of the building's volume, with 4,200 seats spread across three seating levels.

facts.fact: Frank Lloyd Wright, who joined Adler & Sullivan in 1887, helped work on the design.
facts.quote: Frank Lloyd Wright, who joined Adler & Sullivan that year, helped work on the design.

facts.fact: It is a Chicago Landmark and a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: The building is a Chicago Landmark and a National Historic Landmark, and it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: The Climatron is a greenhouse in a geodesic dome at the Missouri Botanical Garden in St. Louis.
facts.quote: The Climatron is a greenhouse enclosed in a geodesic dome that is part of the Missouri Botanical Garden in St. Louis.

facts.fact: It was the world's first fully air-conditioned greenhouse and the first geodesic dome enclosed in rigid Plexiglas panels.
facts.quote: Initiated by then Garden director Frits W. Went, the dome is the world's first completely air-conditioned greenhouse and the first geodesic dome to be enclosed in rigid Plexiglass (Perspex) panels.

facts.fact: Completed in 1960, it was designed by T. C. Howard of Synergetics, Inc.
facts.quote: Completed in 1960, it was designed by T. C. Howard, of Synergetics, Inc., Raleigh, North Carolina.

facts.fact: It is an unpartitioned half-sphere 42 m across and 21 m high.
facts.quote: The structure is an unpartitioned half-sphere dome, 42 m in diameter and 21 m high.

facts.fact: Its frame works with aluminium tubes in compression and aluminium rods in tension.
facts.quote: The frame is supported by aluminum tubes under compression and aluminum rods under tension.

facts.fact: Climate controls, not interior partitions, create the range of climates inside, recreating a lowland rainforest.
facts.quote: The broad climatic range within the dome, which recreates a lowland rain forest, is achieved by sophisticated climate controls without using interior partitions.

facts.fact: Its architects won the 1961 R. S. Reynolds Memorial Award for their use of aluminium.
facts.quote: The architects received the 1961 R. S. Reynolds Memorial Award of $25,000 for their architectural use of aluminum.

facts.fact: In 1976 it was named one of the 100 most significant architectural achievements in United States history.
facts.quote: In 1976 it was named one of the 100 most significant architectural achievements in United States history.

facts.fact: In a 1988–1990 renovation its Plexiglas was replaced with 2,425 panes of heat-strengthened glass with a low-emissivity coating.
facts.quote: The original Plexiglas glazing was replaced with 2,425 panes of heat-strengthened glass (containing a plastic interlayer called Saflex) and coated with a low-emissivity film.

facts.fact: Biosphere 2 is an Earth system science research facility of the University of Arizona in Oracle, Arizona.
facts.quote: University of Arizona Biosphere 2 is an American Earth system science research facility located in Oracle, Arizona.

facts.fact: Its 1.27-hectare structure was built as an artificial, materially closed ecological system and remains the largest ever created.
facts.quote: It is a 3.14-acre (1.27-hectare) structure originally built to be an artificial, materially closed ecological system, or vivarium. It remains the largest closed ecological system ever created.

facts.fact: Built between 1987 and 1991, it was meant to test whether closed ecological systems could support human life in outer space.
facts.quote: Constructed between 1987 and 1991, Biosphere 2 planned to experiment with the viability of closed ecological systems to support and maintain human life in outer space as a substitute for Earth's biosphere.

facts.fact: Its biomes included a rainforest, an ocean with a coral reef, mangrove wetlands, savannah grassland and fog desert, plus a farm and a human habitat.
facts.quote: Its seven biome areas included a 1,900-square-meter (20,000 sq ft) rainforest, an 850-square-meter (9,100 sq ft) ocean with a coral reef, a 450-square-meter (4,800 sq ft) mangrove wetlands, a 1,300-square-metre (14,000 sq ft) savannah grassland, and a 1,400-square-meter (15,000 sq ft) fog desert. it also housed two anthropogenic biomes; a 2,500-square-meter (27,000 sq ft) agricultural system and a human habitat with living spaces, laboratories and workshops.

facts.fact: Above ground it is built of steel tubing, high-performance glass and steel frames.
facts.quote: The above-ground physical structure of Biosphere 2 is made of steel tubing, high-performance glass and steel frames.

facts.fact: The frame and glazing were designed and made by Pearce Structures, the firm of Peter Jon Pearce, an associate of Buckminster Fuller.
facts.quote: The frame and glazing materials were designed and made to specification by a firm run by an associate of Buckminster Fuller, Peter Jon Pearce (Pearce Structures, Inc.).

facts.fact: Patented airtight seals developed by Pearce and William Dempster kept the leak rate below 10% a year.
facts.quote: The patented airtight sealing methods, developed by Pearce and William Dempster, achieved a leak rate of less than 10% per year.

facts.fact: To cope with air expanding by day and contracting by night, it has large diaphragms in domes called 'lungs'.
facts.quote: To avoid dealing with the huge forces created by maintaining a constant volume, the structure had large diaphragms kept in domes called "lungs" or variable volume structures.

facts.fact: At risk of demolition, it was taken over for research by the University of Arizona in 2007.
facts.quote: The facility was at risk of demolition but was taken over for research by the University of Arizona in 2007.

facts.fact: The Denver Central Library is the flagship of the Denver Public Library system.
facts.quote: The Denver Central Library is the flagship building of the Denver Public Library System.

facts.fact: It stands in Downtown Denver's Golden Triangle, next to the Denver Art Museum.
facts.quote: It is located within Downtown Denver's Golden Triangle neighborhood and sits on the south side of Colorado's 16th Street Mall, adjacent to the Denver Art Museum.

facts.fact: The postmodern building was designed by Michael Graves.
facts.quote: The postmodern building was designed by architect Michael Graves.

facts.fact: Commissioned in 1990 and completed in 1995, it is one of the largest libraries in the United States.
facts.quote: Commissioned in 1990 and completed in 1995, it is one of the largest libraries in the United States and receives more than one million visitors each year.

facts.fact: Paid for by a $91.6 million bond to add onto the Fisher/Hoyt library, the 540,000-square-foot (50,000 m²) building by Graves and the Denver firm Klipp Colussy Jenks DuBois opened in 1995.
facts.quote: In the 1990s Denver voters approved a $91.6 million bond issue to add onto the Fisher/Hoyt building; the new 540,000-square-foot (50,000 m2) structure, designed by the 2012 Driehaus Prize winner Michael Graves and the Denver firm of Klipp Colussy Jenks DuBois, opened in 1995.

facts.fact: Its seven-storey exterior is finished in limestone and precast concrete with copper accents.
facts.quote: The seven-story exterior is finished with limestone and pre-cast concrete with copper accents throughout.

facts.fact: Its design uses postmodern motifs: abstracted classical forms, colours and materials from the past.
facts.quote: The 540,000-square-foot (50,000 m2) post-modern design takes use of traditional post-modern motifs of abstracted classical forms, colors, and materials from the past.

facts.fact: Inside are murals by Edward Ruscha, and fossils are set into the floor of Schlessman Hall.
facts.quote: Murals are painted inside by the artist Edward Ruscha and fossils are embedded in its floor within the Schlessman Hall.

facts.fact: It hosted the 23rd G8 Summit in 1997.
facts.quote: It was the venue of the 23rd G8 Summit in 1997.

facts.fact: The Allen–Lambe House is a Prairie Style home in Wichita, Kansas, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1915 for the former Kansas governor Henry Justin Allen and his wife Elsie.
facts.quote: The Allen–Lambe House (also known as the Henry J. Allen House and the Allen House) is a Prairie Style home in Wichita, Kansas, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1915 for former Kansas Governor Henry Justin Allen and his wife, Elsie.

facts.fact: It was one of Wright's last Prairie Houses.
facts.quote: It was one of Frank Lloyd Wright's last Prairie Houses.

facts.fact: Both the prairie and Japanese architecture influenced its exterior and interior; Wright was working on the Imperial Hotel in Japan at the time.
facts.quote: The design influence of the prairie and Japanese architecture (Wright was working on the Imperial Hotel in Japan at the time) is apparent on both the exterior and interior.

facts.fact: Outside, a horizontal grey Carthage marble water table links the ground and the house, with white horizontal brick joints and flush ochre head joints.
facts.quote: The building's exterior features a horizontal grey Carthage marble water table as a transitional element between the ground and the house, white horizontal brick joints and flush ocher head joints.

facts.fact: The roof stresses horizontal lines and is covered in Ludowici tiles with a Japanese-inspired starting course.
facts.quote: The roof was designed with an emphasis on horizontal lines and covered with Ludowici tiles, featuring a unique Japanese-inspired starting course.

facts.fact: The living and dining rooms wrap around a sunken garden with lilies and koi.
facts.quote: The living and dining rooms wrap around a sunken garden filled with lilies and koi fish.

facts.fact: It had the first firewall in a residential home.
facts.quote: Another innovation was the first firewall in a residential home.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 7 March 1973.
facts.quote: The house was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on March 7, 1973.

facts.fact: The Dreischeibenhaus ('three slabs building') is a 95-metre office building in the Hofgarten district of central Düsseldorf.
facts.quote: The Dreischeibenhaus (English: "Three plates building", also known as the Dreischeibenhochhaus) is a 95-metre office building in August-Thyssen-Straße in the Hofgarten district of the Düsseldorf city centre.

facts.fact: It was also called the Thyssenhaus, as it was the headquarters of the Thyssen and ThyssenKrupp groups.
facts.quote: It was also known as the Thyssenhaus or Thyssen-Hochhaus owing to its former use as the headquarters of the Thyssen and ThyssenKrupp groups.

facts.fact: Helmut Hentrich built it from 1957 to 1960, and it remains one of Germany's best-known and most important high-rise buildings.
facts.quote: Hentrich gained worldwide recognition with the construction of the Dreischeibenhaus from 1957 to 1960; with its significant appearance, the building is still one of the best-known and most important high-rise buildings in Germany.

facts.fact: It is among the most significant examples of post-war modernist International Style and a symbol of Germany's post-war 'economic miracle'.
facts.quote: It is among the most significant examples of post-war modernist International style and a symbol of the so-called Wirtschaftswunder, or 'economic miracle' of post-war Germany, and contrasts with the neighbouring Düsseldorfer Schauspielhaus on Gustaf-Gründgens-Platz.

facts.fact: It was one of the first skyscrapers completed in Germany after the Second World War.
facts.quote: Dreischeibenhaus, The "Three Plates Building" (a rough translation of its name in German), was one of the first skyscrapers to be completed in Germany after WW2.

facts.fact: In the early 1990s it was refurbished with a new curtain wall that matches the original but performs better against heat and moisture.
facts.quote: In the early 1990s the building was completely refurbished including a new curtain wall matching the appearance of the original, but with improved thermal performance and moisture control.

facts.fact: After another full renovation by HPP Architects in 2013, it offers 35,000 square metres of gross floor area.
facts.quote: After another complete renovation under the direction of Düsseldorf HPP Architects in 2013, the skyscraper now offers 35,000 m2 of gross floor area.

facts.fact: The Detlev-Rohwedder-Haus in Berlin was the largest office building in Europe when it was built.
facts.quote: The Detlev-Rohwedder-Haus (Detlev Rohwedder House) is a building in Berlin that, at the time of its construction, was the largest office building in Europe.

facts.fact: It was built between February 1935 and August 1936 for the German Ministry of Aviation, headed by Hermann Göring.
facts.quote: It was constructed between February 1935 and August 1936 to house the German Ministry of Aviation (German: Reichsluftfahrtministerium - RLM), headed by Hermann Göring.

facts.fact: It was designed by Ernst Sagebiel, who rebuilt Tempelhof Airport on a similarly gigantic scale.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Ernst Sagebiel, who rebuilt Tempelhof Airport on a similarly gigantic scale.

facts.fact: Sagebiel's austere, stark and linear style was described as 'Luftwaffe modern'.
facts.quote: Sagebiel's austere building style, which when compared to Albert Speer's rather classicist tendencies came across as very stark and linear, was described as "Luftwaffe modern", owing to his close association with the Luftwaffe.

facts.fact: It has a reinforced concrete skeleton faced in limestone and travertine.
facts.quote: It comprised a reinforced concrete skeleton with an exterior facing of limestone and travertine.

facts.fact: It has seven storeys, 112,000 square metres of floor space, 2,800 rooms, 7 km of corridors and over 4,000 windows.
facts.quote: With its seven storeys and total floor area of 112,000 square metres (1,210,000 sq ft), 2,800 rooms, 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) of corridors, over 4,000 windows, 17 stairways, and with the stone coming from no fewer than 50 quarries, the vast building served the growing bureaucracy of the Luftwaffe, plus Germany's civil aviation authority which was also located there.

facts.fact: It took only 18 months to build, with labourers working double shifts and Sundays.
facts.quote: Yet it took only 18 months to build, the army of labourers working double shifts and Sundays.

facts.fact: The German Democratic Republic was founded in a ceremony in its Festsaal on 7 October 1949.
facts.quote: On 7 October 1949, the German Democratic Republic (GDR) was founded in a ceremony in the Festsaal, with Wilhelm Pieck as President and Otto Grotewohl as Prime Minister (Ministerpräsident).

facts.fact: Since 1999, after extensive refurbishment, it has been the headquarters of the German Finance Ministry.
facts.quote: From 1990, the Berlin branch office of the German Finance Ministry was also located there, and since 1999, following extensive refurbishment, the building has served as the Ministry's headquarters.

facts.fact: The Stockholm Court House (Stockholms rådhus) stands on Kungsholmen in central Stockholm.
facts.quote: The Stockholm Court House (Swedish: Stockholms rådhus) is situated on Kungsholmen in Central Stockholm, Sweden.

facts.fact: It housed the Stockholm City Court from 1915 to 1971 and the Stockholm District Court since 1971.
facts.quote: The Stockholm City Court was situated in the building from 1915 to 1971 and Stockholm District Court from 1971.

facts.fact: It was designed in the National Romantic style and built between 1909 and 1915.
facts.quote: The building was designed in the National Romantic style, and was constructed between 1909 and 1915.

facts.fact: It is one of the prominent examples of Carl Westman's National Romantic style, after his Swedish General Medical Association building.
facts.quote: Carl Westman's Swedish General Medical Association building in Stockholm (1904-1906) was the first building built in the National Romantic Style, with the Röhss Museum in Gothenburg (1910–1914) and Stockholm Court House (1911–1915), providing another two prominent examples.

facts.fact: Its architecture was influenced by the castles of the Vasa era and resembles Vadstena Castle.
facts.quote: The architecture was influenced by the Castles of the Vasa era, and it bears a resemblance to Vadstena Castle.

facts.fact: It is a striking sight in downtown Stockholm, though the building proves quite inflexible for its purposes.
facts.quote: The Stockholm Court House has striking similarities with the medieval Vadstena Castle, and provides a dazzling sight in downtown Stockholm, though the building proves quite inflexible for its purposes.

facts.fact: Westman was one of the first Swedish architects to develop the Nordic National Romantic style, which merged local building traditions with Arts and Crafts ideas, often in brick and wood.
facts.quote: He was one of the first Swedish architects who developed the new Nordic National Romantic Style, a style which took the cultural and building precedents and merged them with ideas from the English Arts and Crafts movement to create a very distinct Swedish architecture often in brick and wood.

facts.fact: The Military Cathedral of St. Mary Queen of Peace is a Roman Catholic church in Brasília, the capital of Brazil.
facts.quote: The Military Cathedral of St. Mary Queen of Peace (also Military Cathedral of Brasília; Portuguese: Catedral Militar Santa Maria dos Militares Rainha da Paz) is a Roman Catholic church in the city of Brasília, the capital of Brazil.

facts.fact: It stands on the west side of the Monumental Axis, close to the Urban Military Sector.
facts.quote: It is located on the west side, between the N1 and S1 tracks of the Monumental Axis, close to the Urban Military Sector (SMU).

facts.fact: It was designed by Oscar Niemeyer and inaugurated on 12 September 1994.
facts.quote: It was designed by the Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer and inaugurated on September 12, 1994.

facts.fact: It belongs to the Military Ordinariate of Brazil.
facts.quote: It belongs to the Military Ordinariate of Brazil and has as archbishop Marcony Vinícius Ferreira.

facts.fact: Its triangular form refers to a tent.
facts.quote: Its architecture in triangular format refers to a tent.

facts.fact: Pope John Paul II laid its foundation stone in 1991.
facts.quote: Pope John Paul II laid the foundation stone in 1991 during his visit to Brazil.

facts.fact: The Stephanuskirche, also called Detmerode Church, is a church and parish centre in Wolfsburg, Germany, designed by Alvar Aalto in 1963.
facts.quote: Stephanuskirche (Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Stephen) also known as Detmerode Church is a church and parish center in Wolfsburg, Germany designed by Finnish architect Alvar Aalto in 1963.

facts.fact: Completed in 1968, it is a prominent example of International modernism in Germany.
facts.quote: Completed in 1968, the building is a prominent example of International modernism in Germany.

facts.fact: It has 250 seats and can be arranged to hold 600.
facts.quote: The church contains 250 seats and can be configured to hold a capacity of 600 when needed.

facts.fact: The A. D. German Warehouse is a Mayan Revival warehouse by Frank Lloyd Wright in Richland Center, Wisconsin, built in 1921.
facts.quote: The A. D. German Warehouse is a Frank Lloyd Wright–designed Mayan Revival warehouse that was constructed in Richland Center, Wisconsin in 1921.

facts.fact: Wright was born in Richland Center in 1867.
facts.quote: Wright was born in Richland Center in 1867.

facts.fact: Wright designed it instead of paying a bill he owed to Albert Delvino German.
facts.quote: Wright designed the warehouse in lieu of a required bill payment to Albert Delvino German.

facts.fact: It was designed for storing and selling wholesale goods, with plans for a teahouse restaurant, shops and an art gallery; construction ran from 1917 to 1921.
facts.quote: Designed for "storing and selling wholesale goods", the space was to include a "teahouse restaurant, retail shops, and an art gallery." Construction on the building began in 1917 with completion in 1921.

facts.fact: It is mostly concrete, faced in brick, with a Mayan-inspired concrete frieze derived from masks of the rain-god Chac.
facts.quote: Facing one of the main streets in Richland Center, the building is mostly concrete, veneered in brick with a Mayan-inspired concrete frieze "derived from masks of the rain-god Chac".

facts.fact: It is on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: The building is on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: A condition assessment and preservation plan were made for the building in 2017.
facts.quote: A condition assessment was performed and preservation plan was created for the building in 2017.

facts.fact: The National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo (MOMAT) is the foremost museum collecting and showing modern Japanese art.
facts.quote: The National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo (東京国立近代美術館, Tōkyō Kokuritsu Kindai Bijutsukan), also known as MOMAT, is the foremost museum collecting and exhibiting modern Japanese art.

facts.fact: It is in Chiyoda, Tokyo, and is known for its 20th-century collection, including Western-style and Nihonga artists.
facts.quote: The museum, in Chiyoda, Tokyo, Japan, is known for its collection of 20th-century art and includes Western-style and Nihonga artists.

facts.fact: It was Japan's first national museum of art, founded in 1952.
facts.quote: The National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo, was the first national museum of art in Japan and dates back to 1952, when it was established as an institution governed by the Ministry of Education.

facts.fact: Kunio Maekawa was the architect of the museum building.
facts.quote: The architect of the building was Kunio Maekawa.

facts.fact: Twice, neighbouring sites were bought and the museum was enlarged.
facts.quote: On two later occasions, neighbouring premises were purchased and the museum was enlarged.

facts.fact: Its most recent redesign was by Yoshirō Taniguchi, father of Yoshio Taniguchi, who designed the extension of MoMA in New York.
facts.quote: The most recent redesign of MOMAT was conceived by Yoshirō Taniguchi (father of Yoshio Taniguchi, who designed the extension of MOMA in New York).

facts.fact: A central aim of Yoshirō Taniguchi's work was using steel and concrete to make modern, earthquake-resistant buildings.
facts.quote: A central focus of his work was the application of steel and concrete to create modern, earthquake-resistant structures.

facts.fact: The Tenerife International Centre for Trade Fairs and Congresses opened in May 1996.
facts.quote: The Tenerife International Centre for Trade Fairs and Congresses (Canary island, Spain), also known as "The Fair Recint" ("Recinto Ferial") was opened in May 1996.

facts.fact: It covers more than 40,000 square metres on the seafront of Santa Cruz de Tenerife.
facts.quote: The building, covers an area exceeding 40,000 square meters in the sea front of Santa Cruz de Tenerife.

facts.fact: Santiago Calatrava designed it as a multipurpose building for fairs, exhibitions and conferences.
facts.quote: The complex was designed by architect and engineer Santiago Calatrava is configured as a multipurpose building that can host major fairs, exhibitions and conferences that take place on the island of Tenerife.

facts.fact: The Great Hall on the top floor covers 12,000 square metres, the largest covered space in the Canary Islands.
facts.quote: The Great Hall, located on the top floor, took a total of 12,000 square meters, making it the largest covered space in the Canary Islands.

facts.fact: The hall is 190 m long, 70 m wide and about 20 m high, built in glass, iron and concrete.
facts.quote: This room, which in turn is the main complex is 190 meters long, 70 wide and about 20 meters in height designed in glass, iron and concrete.

facts.fact: It holds up to 15,000 people.
facts.quote: The maximum capacity reaches 15,000 people.

facts.fact: The annex is reached through an arch 50 metres long.
facts.quote: It is accessible through an arc of 50 meters in length.

facts.fact: It is also the headquarters of the World Trade Center Tenerife.
facts.quote: This building is also the headquarters of the World Trade Center Tenerife.

facts.fact: The Artigas Gardens are a park in La Pobla de Lillet, Barcelona province.
facts.quote: The Artigas Gardens (Catalan: Els Jardins de Can Artigas) are a park in La Pobla de Lillet, Barcelona.

facts.fact: Built in 1905–1906, they were designed by Antoni Gaudí.
facts.quote: Built between 1905 and 1906, they were designed by the Modernista architect Antoni Gaudí.

facts.fact: Gaudí designed them for the textile magnate Joan Artigas i Alart, as thanks for his hospitality while Gaudí stayed in Lillet.
facts.quote: While in Lillet, Gaudí stayed in the house of the textile magnate, Joan Artigas i Alart, who had an estate named Font de la Magnèsia, on the Llobregat river. As thanks for the hospitality of Mr. Artigas, Gaudí designed these gardens for him.

facts.fact: Gaudí sent workers from Park Güell to Lillet, and the two places show clear stylistic and structural similarities.
facts.quote: He sent some of Park Güell's workers to Lillet, and the resulting stylistic and structural similarities between the two locations are obvious.

facts.fact: As at Park Güell, Gaudí fully integrated the gardens with the natural setting.
facts.quote: As he did with Parc Güell, Gaudí designed the Artigas Gardens fully integrated with the surrounding natural environment.

facts.fact: He built an artificial grotto, a typical Gaudí feature.
facts.quote: He also built an artificial grotto, a typical Gaudí hallmark, like the one he had designed for the cascade of the Parc de la Ciutadella.

facts.fact: Symbols of the four gospels appear throughout, such as the eagle of Saint John at the arch bridge over the Llobregat.
facts.quote: For these gardens, he took the symbols from the four gospels. Tetramorph images are found throughout the park: the angel of Saint Matthew at la Cascada; the eagle of Saint John at the Coix arch bridge, which crosses the Llobregat river; the lion of Saint Mark at la Pèrgola; and the bull of Saint Luke at the Bull Fountain.

facts.fact: Practically abandoned by 1971, the gardens were restored in 1992 under the Reial Càtedra Gaudí.
facts.quote: By the end of 1971, the gardens were practically abandoned. In 1992, they were restored under the supervision of the Reial Càtedra Gaudí.

facts.fact: Malmö Opera is an opera house in Malmö, Sweden.
facts.quote: Malmö Opera (Swedish: Malmö opera) is an opera house in Malmö, Sweden.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Sigurd Lewerentz, David Helldén and Erik Lallerstedt.
facts.quote: The new theater building was designed by architects Sigurd Lewerentz, David Helldén and Erik Lallerstedt.

facts.fact: Lewerentz's first proposal in the 1920s was distinctly classical, but it gave way to new trends and the building was designed in the spirit of functionalism.
facts.quote: Sigurd Lewerentz was commissioned in the 1920s to design a new theater in Malmö and proposed a building in a distinctly classical style. However, Lewerentz's original proposal had to give way to new architectural trends in Sweden and the building was designed in the spirit of functionalism.

facts.fact: Built from 1933 to 1944 and inaugurated on 23 September 1944, it was considered the most modern theatre in Northern Europe.
facts.quote: The building was constructed from 1933 to 1944 and was inaugurated on September 23, 1944. The building was considered the most modern theater in Northern Europe.

facts.fact: It combines a functionalist split into several volumes for different uses with a monumental, classical language, notably the marble-clad columns and large windows of the entrance façade.
facts.quote: The theater building combines a functionalist division into several building volumes for different purposes with a monumental design language with classical features, in particular the grand entrance facade's marble-clad columns and large window areas.

facts.fact: With 1,511 seats it is one of the largest auditoriums in Scandinavia, shaped as an enclosed amphitheatre to give the best possible views.
facts.quote: Built 1933-1944 by architect Sigurd Lewerentz and, until 1992, known as the Malmö City Theatre accommodating several different organizations, the Opera House is one of the largest auditoriums in Scandinavia with 1,511 seats, created in the form of an enclosed amphitheatre in order to allow for the greatest viewing possibility.

facts.fact: Retractable walls can reduce the auditorium to four different sizes.
facts.quote: The auditorium can be reduced to four different sizes by means of retractable walls.

facts.fact: Influenced by the director Max Reinhardt, a revolving stage 20 metres across was built.
facts.quote: Influenced by German director Max Reinhardt, a large (20 meters in diameter) revolving stage was constructed.

facts.fact: It has been a listed building since 13 December 1994.
facts.quote: Since December 13, 1994, the theater is a listed building.

facts.fact: It is regarded as one of the masterpieces of functionalist architecture.
facts.quote: Between 1933 and 1944 Lewerentz, together with his colleagues Erik Lallerstedt and David Helldén, created what is regarded of one of the masterpieces of functionalist architecture, Malmö Opera and Music Theatre (Malmö Opera och Musikteater).

facts.fact: Cecil H. Green Library is the main library on the Stanford University campus.
facts.quote: The Cecil H. Green Library (commonly known as Green Library) is the main library on the Stanford University campus and is part of the SUL system.

facts.fact: It holds 4 million volumes, mostly in the humanities and social sciences.

facts.quote: The fire was so severe because the building was not equipped with a sprinkler system, which was not required for office towers at the time of its construction.

facts.fact: After the fire, Los Angeles changed its building codes to require fire sprinklers in all high-rises.
facts.quote: Because of the fire, building codes in Los Angeles were modified, requiring all high-rises to be equipped with fire sprinklers.

facts.fact: The Coliseum Theater is a former cinema in Seattle that opened on 8 January 1916.
facts.quote: The Coliseum Theater, a former cinema in Seattle, Washington, opened January 8, 1916.

facts.fact: It is on the National Register of Historic Places (1975) and is an official Seattle city landmark.
facts.quote: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975, and is also an official Seattle city landmark.

facts.fact: Designed by B. Marcus Priteca, it was Seattle's first theatre built for showing films and one of the first cinemas anywhere to aim for architectural grandeur.
facts.quote: Designed by B. Marcus Priteca, it was Seattle's first theater built specifically for showing movies, and was one of the first cinemas anywhere to strive for architectural grandeur.

facts.fact: In 1931 the Journal of the Royal Institute of Architects called it the first of the world's movie palaces.
facts.quote: In 1931, the Journal of the Royal Institute of Architects called it "the first of the world's movie palaces."

facts.fact: The outside has elaborate terracotta work, and the original interior was just as ornate.
facts.quote: The exterior features elaborate terra cotta work, and the original interior was comparably ornate.

facts.fact: It closed as a cinema in 1990 and was turned into a Banana Republic clothing store that opened in 1994.
facts.quote: It closed on March 11, 1990, after showing the film Tremors; the building was renovated into a 15,000-square-foot (1,400 m2) Banana Republic clothing store that opened in 1994.

facts.fact: The crematorium at Brno Central Cemetery was built by Ernst Wiesner in the Functionalist style in 1926–1929 and has been a national cultural monument since 2017.
facts.quote: Since 2017, the crematorium, which was built by Ernst Wiesner in the Functionalist style in 1926–1929, is also protected as a national cultural monument.

facts.fact: The B.J. Ricker House is a historic house in Grinnell, Iowa.
facts.quote: The B.J. Ricker House is a historic dwelling located in Grinnell, Iowa, United States.

facts.fact: It matters as an early example of Walter Burley Griffin's work.
facts.quote: The significance of this house is that it is an early example of Walter Burley Griffin's work.

facts.fact: Building began in 1911, but problems with millwork and labour delayed completion to 1912.
facts.quote: Construction on the house began in 1911, but millwork and labor problems pushed its completion to 1912.

facts.fact: The two-storey brick house has a rectangular plan, a high cement basement, broad brick piers at the four corners and a gable roof that seems to hover over the main block.
facts.quote: The two-story brick house features a rectangular plan, a high cement basement, four broad brick piers on the corners, and a gable roof that appears to hover over the main block.

facts.fact: The veranda on the south side follows a Greek cross plan.
facts.quote: The veranda on the south side of the house follows a Greek cross plan.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
facts.quote: The house was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

facts.fact: The Alcide De Gasperi building is a skyscraper in Kirchberg, in the north-east of Luxembourg City.
facts.quote: The Alcide De Gasperi building (named after Italian statesman Alcide De Gasperi) is a skyscraper in Kirchberg, north-eastern Luxembourg City, in southern Luxembourg.

facts.fact: At 77 m and 23 floors it was Luxembourg's first skyscraper and its tallest building, nicknamed Héichhaus ('High House').
facts.quote: At 77 m (253 ft) tall and with 23 floors, it was the first skyscraper and the tallest building in Luxembourg, and was thus dubbed Héichhaus ('High House') in Luxembourgish.

facts.fact: It was built in 1966 to house the Secretariat of the European Parliament.
facts.quote: It was built in 1966 to house the Secretariat of the European Parliament.

facts.fact: Villa Savoye is a modernist villa in Poissy, outside Paris, designed by Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret, with interiors by Charlotte Perriand, and built in reinforced concrete between 1928 and 1931.
facts.quote: It was designed by the Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier and his cousin Pierre Jeanneret with interior and furnishing by Charlotte Perriand, and built between 1928 and 1931 using reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: It was built as a country retreat for the Savoye family.
facts.quote: The house was originally built as a country retreat for the Savoye family.

facts.fact: Its design embodied Le Corbusier's Five Points, the basic rules of his new architecture.
facts.quote: Its design embodied his emblematic "Five Points", the basic tenets in his new architectural aesthetic:

facts.fact: Because it stood alone in the country, Le Corbusier could design all four sides around the view and the path of the sun.
facts.quote: Unlike with his earlier town villas, Le Corbusier was able to carefully design all four sides of the Villa Savoye so that they took the view and the orientation of the sun into account.

facts.fact: The plan was set out with the ratios of the golden section: a square divided into sixteen equal parts.
facts.quote: The plan was set out using the principal ratios of the Golden section: in this case a square divided into sixteen equal parts, extended on two sides to incorporate the projecting façades, and then further divided so as to fix the position of the ramp and the entrance.

facts.fact: The curve of the ground-floor glazing was set by the turning circle of a car.
facts.quote: Even the curved arc of the industrial glazing of the ground floor entrance was determined by the turning circle of a car.

facts.fact: A ramp, visible from almost everywhere in the house, rises from the entrance hall to the first-floor living area and on outside to the rooftop solarium.
facts.quote: This ramp, which can be seen from almost everywhere in the house, continues up to the first-floor living area and salon before continuing externally from the first-floor roof terrace up to the second-floor solarium.

facts.fact: In 2016 the house and 16 other Le Corbusier buildings in seven countries were inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: In July 2016, the house and 16 other buildings by Le Corbusier, spread over seven countries, were inscribed as The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

facts.fact: The president of the Ahmedabad Mill Owners' Association commissioned Le Corbusier to build its new headquarters, finished in 1954.
facts.quote: Surottam Hutheesing, then president of Ahmedabad Mill Owners' Association, commissioned Corbusier to build the new headquarters of the association. It was completed in 1954.

facts.fact: A ceremonial ramp leads up into a triple-height entrance hall open to the wind.
facts.quote: A ceremonial ramp makes for a grand approach into a triple height entrance hall, open to the wind.

facts.fact: The top floor holds a high, top-lit auditorium with a roof canopy and a curved enclosing wall.
facts.quote: On the third floor is a high, top-lit auditorium with a roof canopy and a curved, enclosing wall, in addition to a generous lobby.

facts.fact: The east and west fronts are brise-soleil that keep out harsh sun while letting in views and moving air.
facts.quote: The east and west façades are in the form of sun breakers or brise-soleil, one of Corbusier's many formal inventions, which, while avoiding harsh sun, permit visual connection and air movement.

facts.fact: The brise-soleil are rough shuttered concrete, while the north and south sides are almost unbroken rough brickwork.
facts.quote: While the brise-soleil act as free façades made of rough shuttered concrete, the north and south sides, built in rough brickwork, are almost unbroken.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier expressed the association's public and private sides through his idea of the house as a palace.
facts.quote: Corbusier expressed the institution's dual character - the public and the private - through his concept of the house as a palace (Une maison - un palais).

facts.fact: Later projects, notably the Carpenter Center at Harvard, drew on experiments made in this building.
facts.quote: Conversely, many of his later projects, most notably the Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts at Harvard, benefited from some of the experiments carried out in this particular building.

facts.fact: Mies van der Rohe designed the Farnsworth House near Plano, Illinois, completed in 1951, as a weekend retreat for the physician Edith Farnsworth.
facts.quote: Completed in 1951, it was designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe in the International Style and built as a weekend retreat for the nephrologist and physician Edith Farnsworth.

facts.fact: The house is raised 1.6 m above the Fox River floodplain, with a minimal exterior and a mostly open plan inside.
facts.quote: The house is raised 5+1⁄4 feet (1.6 m) above the floodplain, with a minimalist exterior and a mostly open plan interior.

facts.fact: Eight steel columns carry the concrete floor and roof slabs and divide the house into three bays.
facts.quote: The concrete floor and roof slabs are supported by eight steel columns, which divide the house into three west–east bays.

facts.fact: The walls are glass between steel mullions, and the western third of the house is an open-air veranda.
facts.quote: The facade is composed of glass, interspersed with steel mullions; the western third of the house is an open-air veranda.

facts.fact: The open interior is broken only by an off-centre core and a movable wardrobe.
facts.quote: The interior has a minimalist color scheme and is interrupted only by an off-center utility core and a movable wardrobe.

facts.fact: The core holds the kitchen, bathrooms and services, with living, dining and sleeping areas placed around it.
facts.quote: The core contains utilities, a kitchen, and bathrooms, while living, dining, and sleeping areas are placed around it.

facts.fact: It is a National Historic Landmark, and its design influenced other houses and Mies's later work.
facts.quote: The house has been the subject of books, films, exhibits, and other media works and is designated as a National Historic Landmark. Its design has influenced that of other houses and Mies's later work.

facts.fact: Crown Hall, completed in 1956, was designed by Mies van der Rohe for IIT's College of Architecture in Chicago, which he led.
facts.quote: Completed in 1956, the structure was designed by the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe for the IIT's College of Architecture, which he led for two decades.

facts.fact: It is a Chicago Landmark and a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: Crown Hall is a Chicago Landmark and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as a National Historic Landmark.

facts.fact: The glass curtain wall is divided into three tiers of panes between steel columns and mullions.
facts.quote: The glass curtain wall is divided horizontally into three tiers of panes, interspersed with steel columns and mullions.

facts.fact: The roof, 5.5 m above the main floor, hangs from four girders resting on four pairs of columns.
facts.quote: The roof is 18 feet (5.5 m) above the main level and is supported by four girders, which rest on four pairs of columns.

facts.fact: Inside, the main floor is a mostly open space with half-height partitions and no interior columns apart from two service shafts.
facts.quote: Inside, the main level is a mostly open plan space with half-height partitions; there are no interior columns besides two mechanical shafts.

facts.fact: Apart from the entrances, the exterior is made entirely of steel and glass.
facts.quote: Except for the areas around the entrances, the exterior is made entirely of steel and glass.

facts.fact: Renovations in the 2000s fixed design problems, upgraded the services and made the building more energy efficient.
facts.quote: Extensive renovations in the 2000s fixed issues with the design, upgraded mechanical systems, and made the building more energy efficient.

facts.fact: The Seagram Building is a 38-storey, 157 m office tower on Park Avenue in Manhattan, completed in 1958 as the headquarters of the distiller Seagram.
facts.quote: The high-rise tower is 515 feet (157 m) tall with 38 stories and, when completed in 1958, initially served as the headquarters of the Seagram Company, a Canadian distiller.

facts.fact: Mies van der Rohe designed it in the International Style with Philip Johnson, Ely Jacques Kahn and Robert Allan Jacobs.
facts.quote: It was designed in the International Style by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe along with Philip Johnson, Ely Jacques Kahn, and Robert Allan Jacobs.

facts.fact: Phyllis Lambert, daughter of Seagram's chief executive, strongly shaped the design.
facts.quote: Phyllis Lambert, daughter of Seagram CEO Samuel Bronfman, heavily influenced the Seagram Building's design, an example of the functionalist aesthetic and a prominent instance of corporate modern architecture.

facts.fact: The tower stands back 90 feet from Park Avenue, leaving half the site as a plaza.
facts.quote: The Seagram Building occupies half the site and is recessed 90 feet (27 m) behind Park Avenue.

facts.fact: It was the first office building in the world with extruded bronze on its facade, and the first New York skyscraper with full-height plate glass windows.
