facts.quote: The Seagram Building was the first office building in the world to use extruded bronze on a facade, as well as the first New York City skyscraper with full-height plate glass windows.

facts.fact: Its plaza helped shape New York's 1961 Zoning Resolution, which gave developers extra floor area in return for public plazas.
facts.quote: Within New York City, the Seagram Building helped influence the 1961 Zoning Resolution, a zoning ordinance that allowed developers to construct additional floor area in exchange for including plazas outside their buildings.

facts.fact: Its exterior, lobby and Four Seasons Restaurant were made New York City landmarks in 1989.
facts.quote: In 1989, the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Seagram Building's exterior, lobby, and The Four Seasons Restaurant as official city landmarks.

facts.fact: The Neue Nationalgalerie is Berlin's museum of 20th-century art; Mies van der Rohe designed the building and its sculpture gardens, which opened in 1968.
facts.quote: The museum building and its sculpture gardens were designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and opened on 15 September 1968 in what was then West Berlin south of the Tiergarten park.

facts.fact: Eight cruciform columns, kept away from the corners, carry a square steel roof plate 1.8 m thick, painted black.
facts.quote: Eight cruciform columns, two on each length placed so as to avoid corners, support a square pre-stressed steel roof plate 1.8 meters (5 ft 11 in) thick and painted black.

facts.fact: An 18 m cantilever leaves wide space between the glass walls and the eight columns.
facts.quote: An 18-meter (59-foot) cantilever allows for ample space between the gallery's glazed façade and eight supporting columns.

facts.fact: The glass hall is 8.4 m high and laid out on a 3.6 m square grid.
facts.quote: The floor-to-ceiling height reaches 8.4 meters (28 ft), and the space is (laid) out on a 3.6-meter (12 ft) square dimensional grid.

facts.fact: The permanent collection sits in a lower storey, three-quarters below ground, to keep the artworks safe.
facts.quote: It is three-quarters below ground so as to allow for safe storage of the artwork.

facts.fact: The Neue Nationalgalerie is the only built version of three closely related Mies designs, refined through repeated reworking.
facts.quote: Though the Schweinfurt project never came to fruition, the reductive exercise of continual reconfiguration led to a refinement of Mies' Berlin design, and the Neue Nationalgalerie remains as the sole built form of the three related plans.

facts.fact: David Chipperfield Architects renovated it from 2015, and it reopened in August 2021.
facts.quote: The work, by David Chipperfield Architects, was completed in 2021, and the museum reopened in August 2021 with an exhibition of works by American sculptor Alexander Calder.

facts.fact: Frank Lloyd Wright designed the S. C. Johnson headquarters in Racine, Wisconsin: the Administration Building (1939) and the Research Tower (1950).
facts.quote: The original headquarters includes two buildings designed by Frank Lloyd Wright: the Administration Building, completed in April 1939, and the Research Tower, completed in November 1950.

facts.fact: The Administration Building is a variation of streamlined Art Moderne, with a curved brick facade and Pyrex glass-tube windows.
facts.quote: The Johnson Administration Building is designed in a variation of the streamlined Art Moderne style, with a curved brick facade and Pyrex glass-tube windows.

facts.fact: Its main space is a great workroom of concrete columns topped by large 'calyxes'.
facts.quote: The Administration Building's primary interior space is a great workroom with concrete shell columns topped by large "calyxes".

facts.fact: The 15-storey Research Tower alternates square floors with circular mezzanines, cantilevered out from a central core.
facts.quote: The tower has alternating square floors and circular mezzanines, cantilevered outward from the structural core.

facts.fact: A test column carried 60 short tons before it showed any strain, after which Wright had it pulled down.
facts.quote: The column was able to withstand a load of 60 short tons (54 long tons; 54 t) before it showed any strain, at which point Wright ordered workers to pull down the column.

facts.fact: The glass tubes leaked for years after completion.
facts.quote: The caulking between the Administration Building's Pyrex glass tubes began to peel off after it was completed, causing leaks, which continued for several years.

facts.fact: It received the AIA Twenty-five Year Award and is a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: In addition, the original headquarters received the American Institute of Architects' Twenty-five Year Award and has been designated as a National Historic Landmark.

facts.fact: Gerrit Rietveld built the house in Utrecht in 1924 for Truus Schröder-Schräder and her three children.
facts.quote: The Rietveld Schröder House (Dutch: Rietveld Schröderhuis; also known as the Schröder House) in Utrecht (Prins Hendriklaan 50) was built in 1924 by Dutch architect Gerrit Rietveld for Mrs. Truus Schröder-Schräder and her three children.

facts.fact: It is one of the best-known examples of De Stijl architecture, and arguably the only true De Stijl building.
facts.quote: The house is one of the best known examples of De Stijl-architecture and arguably the only true De Stijl building.

facts.fact: The upper floor can be left open or divided into rooms with a system of sliding and revolving panels.
facts.quote: Mrs Schröder, however, felt that as living space it should be usable in either form, open or subdivided. This was achieved with a system of sliding and revolving panels.

facts.fact: The facades are a collage of planes and lines that seem to slide past one another.
facts.quote: The facades are a collage of planes and lines whose components are purposely detached from, and seem to glide past, one another.

facts.fact: Surfaces are white and greys, with black window and door frames and linear elements in primary colours.
facts.quote: Colours were chosen as to strengthen the plasticity of the facades; surfaces in white and shades of grey, black window and doorframes, and a number of linear elements in primary colours.

facts.fact: Concrete proved too expensive, so only the foundations and balconies are concrete; the walls are brick and plaster.
facts.quote: The foundations and the balconies were the only parts of the building that were made out of concrete. The walls were made of brick and plaster.

facts.fact: It has been a listed monument since 1976 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
facts.quote: It is a listed monument since 1976 and UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.

facts.fact: Aino and Alvar Aalto designed Villa Mairea, built in 1938–1939 in Noormarkku, Finland, for Harry and Maire Gullichsen.
facts.quote: Villa Mairea is a villa, guest-house, and rural retreat designed and built by the Finnish modernist architects Aino Aalto and Alvar Aalto for Harry and Maire Gullichsen in Noormarkku, Pori, Finland. The building was constructed in 1938–1939.

facts.fact: The clients told the Aaltos to treat it as 'an experimental house'.
facts.quote: They told the Aaltos that they should regard it as 'an experimental house'.

facts.fact: The plan is a modified L-shape of a kind the Aaltos had used before.
facts.quote: The plan of the Villa Mairea is a modified L-shape of the kind the Aaltos had used before.

facts.fact: Aino Aalto led the interiors, rich in wood, stone and brick, with built-in cabinetry, lighting and textiles.
facts.quote: The interiors of the Villa Mairea were led primarily by Aino Aalto, featuring rich articulation in wood, stone and brick, alongside custom built-in cabinetry, lighting, and textiles.

facts.fact: In the living room the steel columns are irregularly placed, some tripled and clad in wooden strips or bound with rattan.
facts.quote: The dimensions of the structural grid vary in both directions, and the circular steel columns are randomly placed; in one case, they are tripled, clad with wooden strips or bound with rattan, and in the library, one of the three columns is arbitrarily changed to concrete (early sketches also show it as free-form in plan).

facts.fact: Early studies show the influence of Frank Lloyd Wright's Fallingwater, then newly famous.
facts.quote: Early in 1938, however, inspiration came from a radically different source, the residence named 'Fallingwater' designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, which had just received international acclaim thanks to an exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art in New York and publication in Life and Time magazines, as well as in architectural journals.

facts.fact: The critic Sigfried Giedion called it "a love poem" in modern architecture.
facts.quote: Architectural critic Sigfried Giedion famously described the residence as "a love poem" in modern architecture.

facts.fact: In July 2026 it became part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 12 other Aalto works.
facts.quote: In July 2026, Villa Mairea, along with 12 other Aalto Works, was designated by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: The town hall is two main buildings around a central courtyard: a U-shaped council chamber and offices, and a library with flats.
facts.quote: The Säynätsalo Town Hall (Finnish: Säynätsalon kunnantalo) is a multifunction building complex, consisting of two main buildings organised around a central courtyard: a U-shaped council chamber and town hall with administrative offices, and a community library with flats.

facts.fact: Alvar Aalto won the commission in a 1949 design contest, and the building was finished in December 1951.
facts.quote: Aalto received the commission after a design contest in 1949, and the building was completed in December 1951.

facts.fact: Aalto built it into a wooded hillside, three storeys around a raised courtyard.
facts.quote: Aalto constructed the building into the wooded hillside of Säynätsalo creating a three-story multi-purpose building surrounding an elevated courtyard.

facts.fact: The design draws on Finnish vernacular building and the Italian Renaissance.
facts.quote: The design of the Town Hall was influenced by both Finnish vernacular architecture and the humanist Italian renaissance.

facts.fact: The double-height council chamber crowns the building under Aalto's 'butterfly' trusses.
facts.quote: The town hall is crowned by the council chamber, a double-height space which is capped by the Aalto-designed "Butterfly" trusses.

facts.fact: The materials are mostly brick, with timber and copper accents.
facts.quote: Aalto constrained his material palette to one dominated by brick and accented by timber and copper.

facts.fact: The bricks were laid slightly off line so their shadows give the walls a lively surface.
facts.quote: The bricks were even laid slightly off-line to create a dynamic and enlivened surface condition due to the shadows.

facts.fact: Its grass stairs recall ancient Greek and Italian architecture, forming a simple amphitheatre.
facts.quote: The grass stairs also evoke notions of ancient Greek and Italian architecture through the establishment of a form resembling a simple amphitheater condition.

facts.fact: Philip Johnson built the Glass House in New Canaan, Connecticut, in 1948–49 as his own weekend retreat.
facts.quote: It was built in 1948–49 by the architect Philip Johnson, who designed the home as his weekend retreat.

facts.fact: Johnson curated a 1947 exhibition of Mies's work at MoMA that included a model of the Farnsworth House.
facts.quote: Johnson curated an exhibit of Mies's work at the Museum of Modern Art in 1947, featuring a model of the Farnsworth House.

facts.fact: The house is 17 m long, 9.8 m wide and 3.2 m high.
facts.quote: The structure is 56 feet (17 m) long, 32 feet (9.8 m) wide and 10.5 feet (3.2 m) high.

facts.fact: The outside walls are charcoal-painted steel and glass.
facts.quote: The exterior sides of the Glass House utilize charcoal-painted steel and glass.

facts.fact: Low walnut cabinets divide the open interior; a brick cylinder holding the bathroom is the only thing that reaches the ceiling.
facts.quote: The interior is open, with the space divided by low walnut cabinets; a brick cylinder contains the bathroom, the only object to reach floor-to-ceiling.

facts.fact: Johnson called the surrounding landscape his "very expensive wallpaper", part of the idea of removing the barrier between inside and out.
facts.quote: "I have very expensive wallpaper," Johnson once said, of the landscape integral to the home's concept of eliminating the barrier between inside and out.

facts.fact: It was made a National Historic Landmark in 1997 and is run by the National Trust for Historic Preservation.
facts.quote: It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1997. It is now owned by the National Trust for Historic Preservation and is open to the public for guided tours, which begin at a visitors center at 199 Elm Street in New Canaan.

facts.fact: The museum, in Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, documents the atomic bombing of Hiroshima in the Second World War.
facts.quote: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum is a museum in Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, in central Hiroshima, Japan, dedicated to documenting the atomic bombing of Hiroshima in World War II.

facts.fact: Kenzō Tange designed the museum's main building.
facts.quote: The architect of the main building was Kenzō Tange.

facts.fact: Tange, at Tange Lab, also planned and designed the Peace Memorial Park around it.
facts.quote: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park was planned and designed by the Japanese Architect Kenzō Tange at Tange Lab.

facts.fact: The building looks out to the Memorial Cenotaph, the Peace Flame and the A-Bomb Dome.
facts.quote: The building also has views of the Memorial Cenotaph, Peace Flame, and A-Bomb Dome.

facts.fact: The park was built on an open field created by the explosion, in what had been the city's busiest district.
facts.quote: The location of Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park was once the city's busiest downtown commercial and residential district. The park was built on an open field that was created by the explosion.

facts.fact: About 53 million people visited between 1955 and 2005, over a million a year.
facts.quote: 53 million people visited the museum between 1955 and 2005, averaging over one million yearly.

facts.fact: The Main Hall was closed for seismic retrofitting until April 2019.
facts.quote: When the East Wing reopened, the Main Hall was closed for seismic retrofitting until 25 April 2019.

facts.fact: It serves Phillips Exeter Academy in New Hampshire and is the largest secondary school library in the world.
facts.quote: It is the largest secondary school library in the world, containing 160,000 volumes over nine levels with a shelf capacity of 250,000 volumes.

facts.fact: The school chose Louis Kahn in 1965 over a traditional design, and the library opened in 1971.
facts.quote: Deciding instead to construct a library with a contemporary design, the school gave the commission to Louis Kahn in 1965. The library opened in 1971.

facts.fact: Kahn arranged the library as three square rings; the outer one, of load-bearing brick, holds the outside walls and the reading carrels.
facts.quote: Kahn structured the library in three concentric square rings. The outer ring, which is built of load-bearing brick, includes all four exterior walls and the library carrel desks immediately inside them.

facts.fact: The central atrium has huge circular openings that reveal several floors of book stacks.
facts.quote: The inner ring is a dramatic atrium with enormous circular openings in its walls that reveal several floors of book stacks.

facts.fact: The brick piers get thicker towards the bottom, where they carry more weight, and the windows widen towards the top.
facts.quote: Kahn calls this fact to the viewer's attention by making the brick piers noticeably thicker at the bottom where they have more weight to bear. The windows are correspondingly wider toward the top where the piers are thinner.

facts.fact: Two massive concrete cross beams at the top of the atrium spread the light from the clerestory windows.
facts.quote: At the top of the atrium, two massive concrete cross beams diffuse the light entering from the clerestory windows.

facts.fact: Kahn put the reading carrels by the windows: "A man with a book goes to the light."
facts.quote: For Kahn, the essence of a library was the act of taking a book from a shelf and walking a few steps to a window for a closer look: "A man with a book goes to the light. A library begins that way.

facts.fact: It received the AIA's Twenty-five Year Award in 1997.
facts.quote: In 1997 the library received the Twenty-five Year Award from the American Institute of Architects, an award that recognizes architecture of enduring significance that is given to no more than one building per year.

facts.fact: Louis Kahn's Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth is known for the silvery natural light washing across its vaulted gallery ceilings.
facts.quote: It is especially noted for the wash of silvery natural light across its vaulted gallery ceilings.

facts.fact: Building began in summer 1969, and the museum opened in October 1972 to international acclaim.
facts.quote: Construction for the Kimbell Art Museum began in the summer of 1969. The new building opened in October 1972 and quickly achieved an international reputation for architectural excellence.

facts.fact: It is made of 16 parallel vaults, each 30 m long, 6 m high and 6 m wide.
facts.quote: The museum is composed of 16 parallel vaults that are each 100 feet (30.6 m) long, 20 feet (6 m) high and 20 feet (6 m) wide (internal measurements).

facts.fact: Each vault has a slot along its top to let natural light into the galleries.
facts.quote: Each interior vault has a slot along its apex to allow natural light into the galleries.

facts.fact: The cycloid curve of the vaults spreads daylight from the top slot across the whole gallery ceiling.
facts.quote: More importantly, that curve could also be used to produce a beautiful distribution of natural light from a slot in the top of the gallery across the entire gallery ceiling.

facts.fact: Engineer August Komendant used post-tensioned concrete only five inches thick, so the vaults need columns only at their corners.
facts.quote: Komendant was able to use post-tensioned concrete that was only five inches thick to create gallery "vaults" that need support columns only at their four corners.

facts.fact: The concrete-block ends of the vaults are faced in travertine inside and out.
facts.quote: The ends of the vaults, which are made of concrete block, are faced with travertine inside and out.

facts.fact: A separate building by Renzo Piano opened across the lawn in November 2013.
facts.quote: Designed by Renzo Piano, and relocated to the west lawn, the new structure opened to the public in November 2013.

facts.fact: The Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka, Bangladesh's parliament house, was first designed by Louis Kahn for the Parliament of Pakistan and is one of the largest legislative complexes in the world.
facts.quote: Initially designed for the Parliament of Pakistan by architect Louis Kahn, the complex is one of the largest legislative complexes in the world, covering 840,000 m2 (210 acres).

facts.fact: Kahn died when it was about three-quarters built; David Wisdom, who had worked for him, saw it through to completion on 28 January 1982.
facts.quote: Kahn died when the project was approximately three-quarters completed and it continued under David Wisdom, who worked for Kahn. It was completed on 28 January 1982.

facts.fact: Kahn designed the whole complex, including lawns, a lake and residences for MPs, aiming to represent Bengali culture and heritage.
facts.quote: Louis Kahn designed the entire Jatiya Sangsad complex, which includes lawns, lake and residences for the Members of the Parliament (MPs). The architect's key design philosophy was to represent Bengali culture and heritage, while at the same time optimizing the use of space.

facts.fact: Huge walls are cut by deep porticoes and large openings of simple geometric shapes.
facts.quote: The exterior of the building is striking in its simplicity, with huge walls deeply recessed by porticoes and large openings of regular geometric shapes.

facts.fact: An artificial lake on three sides of the main building reflects the river landscape of Bangladesh.
facts.quote: The use of water features is intended to reflect the riverine landscape of Bangladesh and contributes to the site’s overall design.

facts.fact: The building is nine blocks, eight rising to 110 feet around a central octagonal block of 155 feet.
facts.quote: The Bhaban consists of nine individual blocks: the eight peripheral blocks rise to a height of 110' while the central octagonal block rises to a height of 155'.

facts.fact: Daylight reflects off the surrounding walls and octagonal drum and filters into the parliament chamber under its parabolic shell roof.
facts.quote: Daylight, reflecting from the surrounding walls and octagonal drum, filters into the Parliament Chamber.

facts.fact: It received the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1989.
facts.quote: The Parliament building received the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 1989.

facts.fact: The Yale Art and Architecture Building, now Rudolph Hall, houses Yale's School of Architecture and is the Brutalist masterwork of Paul Rudolph, then chair of the department.
facts.quote: The School of Architecture is housed in Rudolph Hall (also known as the Yale Art and Architecture Building), the Brutalist masterwork of former department chair Paul Rudolph.

facts.fact: The school moved into the newly built building in 1963.
facts.quote: In 1963, the School relocated to the newly built Yale Art and Architecture Building (now Rudolph Hall), designed by then Department Chair Paul Rudolph, where it has remained since.

facts.fact: It is a spatially complex Brutalist concrete building, among Rudolph's best-known works.
facts.quote: His best-known works include the Boston Government Service Center and the Yale Art and Architecture Building (A&A Building), a spatially-complex Brutalist concrete structure.

facts.fact: Rudolph's design brought the different fine art departments closely together.
facts.quote: When the Art and Architecture Building became its home, Paul Rudolph's design reflected this close integration between various fine art departments.

facts.fact: It was renovated and expanded in 2008 by a team including Rudolph's former student Charles Gwathmey.
facts.quote: The Yale Art and Architecture Building was extensively renovated and expanded in 2008. The renovation team included New York architect, Yale alumnus, and Rudolph mentee Charles Gwathmey.

facts.fact: The renovation restored its 'original 1963 intention', including historically correct windows.
facts.quote: The interior and exterior renovation restored the structure to its "original 1963 intention," including historically correct windows and upgrades to lighting and furnishings.

facts.fact: Kenzō Tange designed the gymnasium in Tokyo's Yoyogi Park with engineer Yoshikatsu Tsuboi for the 1964 Summer Olympics.
facts.quote: The design of the Yoyogi National Stadium began in 1961 by Kenzō Tange in collaboration with engineer Yoshikatsu Tsuboi. The project was intended for the 1964 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: It took 18 months to build and opened on 10 October 1964.
facts.quote: The bid for the structure was approved 20 months before the start of the games and took 18 months to construct. It was opened on October 10, 1964.

facts.fact: When built, it had the world's largest suspended roof span.
facts.quote: At the time it was built, the gymnasium had the world's largest suspended roof span.

facts.fact: Two reinforced concrete pillars hold a pre-stressed steel net to which steel plates are fixed.
facts.quote: Two reinforced concrete pillars support a pre-stressed steel net onto which steel plates are attached.

facts.fact: The curve of the roof helps protect the building from strong winds.
facts.quote: The overall curvature of the roof helps protect the building from the damaging effects of strong winds.

facts.fact: It inspired the Olympic Stadium for the 1972 Munich Games, and Tange's 1987 Pritzker citation called it among the most beautiful buildings of the 20th century.
facts.quote: Yoyogi National Stadium inspired the design for the Olympic Stadium for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich. In 1987, Kenzō Tange was awarded the Pritzker Architecture Prize, with the citation describing the Yoyogi National Stadium as “among the most beautiful buildings of the 20th century".

facts.fact: In 2021 it was made an Important Cultural Property of Japan.
facts.quote: In 2021, the stadium was designated an Important Cultural Property in Japan for being "a monumental example of postwar architecture with a dynamic exterior and magnificent interior space".

facts.fact: Habitat 67 is a housing complex on the Saint Lawrence River in Montreal, designed by Moshe Safdie.
facts.quote: Habitat 67, or just Habitat, is a housing complex at Cité du Havre, on the Saint Lawrence River, Montreal, Quebec, Canada, designed by Israeli-Canadian-American architect Moshe Safdie.

facts.fact: It began as Safdie's master's thesis at McGill University, and a revised version was built for Expo 67.
facts.quote: It originated in his master's thesis at the School of Architecture at McGill University and then an amended version was built for Expo 67, a World's Fair held from April to October 1967.

facts.fact: It is made of 354 identical prefabricated concrete boxes, arranged in three pyramids up to 12 storeys high.
facts.quote: Habitat 67 comprises 354 identical, prefabricated concrete forms (11.7 m × 5.3 m × 3 m [38 ft 5 in × 17 ft 5 in × 9 ft 10 in]) arranged in various combinations, divided into three pyramids, reaching up to 12 residential storeys, with a parking level, and a building services level.

facts.fact: Every home has at least one private garden terrace, built on the roof of the unit below.
facts.quote: Each unit is connected to at least one private landscaped garden terrace, built on the roof of the level below, which can range from approximately 20 to 90 square metres (225 to 1,000 sq ft) in size.

facts.fact: The aim was to give city apartments the benefits of suburban homes: gardens, fresh air, privacy and many levels.
facts.quote: The development was designed to integrate the benefits of suburban homes—namely gardens, fresh air, privacy, and multilevelled environments—with the economics and density of a modern urban apartment building.

facts.fact: The structural engineer was August Komendant, a pioneer of prestressed concrete.
facts.quote: The structural engineer for the project was August Eduard Komendant, an Estonian-American structural engineer and a pioneer in the field of prestressed concrete.

facts.fact: Safdie's goal of affordable housing largely failed, as demand made the units more expensive than planned.
facts.quote: Safdie's goal for the project to be affordable housing largely failed: demand for the building's units has made them more expensive than originally envisioned.

facts.fact: MASP's building, a 1968 concrete and glass structure by Lina Bo Bardi, is a São Paulo landmark and a symbol of modern Brazilian architecture.
facts.quote: It is well known for the architectural significance of its headquarters, a 1968 concrete and glass structure designed by Lina Bo Bardi. It is considered a landmark of the city and a symbol of modern Brazilian architecture, and one of the most-visited art museums in the world.

facts.fact: To keep the required view over the city, Bo Bardi lifted the building on four huge concrete columns.
facts.quote: To preserve the required view of the downtown area, Bardi idealized a building suspended above ground, supported by four massive rectangular columns made of concrete.

facts.fact: The building stands 8 m above the ground on 4 pillars joined by two huge concrete beams.
facts.quote: The structure stands 8 meters above the ground, supported by 4 pillars connected by two huge concrete beams.

facts.fact: The 74 m free space between the pillars was the largest free span in the world at the time.
facts.quote: A free space of 74 metres (243 ft) between the pillars was the largest free span in the world at that time.

facts.fact: The suspended volume spans 74 m on four bright red concrete columns joined by two beams, with galleries above and below the ground floor.
facts.quote: The building features a suspended volume, spanning 74 meters, held aloft by 4 brilliant red, concrete columns connected by two concrete beam running along the length of the building, with 2 floors of gallery above and below the ground floor.

facts.fact: Paintings hung on sheets of glass set in rough concrete blocks, the 'crystal easels'.
facts.quote: Paintings were hung on individual sheets of glass set in rough-hewn concrete blocks – called "crystal easels" – and arranged in a rough grid in the MASP Pinacoteca.

facts.fact: The building was listed as national heritage in Brazil in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, the building was also registered as national patrimony by Brazilian Institute for Historic and Artistic Heritage.

facts.fact: SESC Pompeia is a cultural and social centre in São Paulo, converted from a former factory by Lina Bo Bardi between 1977 and 1986.
facts.quote: A former factory, the building was converted from 1977 to 1986 by the architect Lina Bo Bardi for the non-profit organization Serviço Social do Comércio (SESC).

facts.fact: The site was a former steel drum and refrigerator factory, turned into a leisure centre for working people, an early example of adaptive reuse.
facts.quote: The Centro de Lazer Fábrica da Pompéia (now called the SESC Pompéia) was one of Bo Bardi's largest and most important projects, in addition to being an early example of adaptive reuse. The site was a former steel drum and refrigerator factory in São Paulo, and was to be redeveloped into a leisure and recreation center for the working class.

facts.fact: Bo Bardi kept the industrial buildings to keep the life local people had already brought to the place.
facts.quote: The project's priority consisted in keeping and amplifying the vitality the neighborhood people had transmitted to the space, so Bo Bardi insisted in keeping the industrial buildings.

facts.fact: She stripped the old plaster and sandblasted to reveal the factory's rough concrete.
facts.quote: Bo Bardi stripped away old plaster and then sandblasted to reveal the rough concrete of the former factory.

facts.fact: Two new concrete towers with sports halls, pierced by irregular round windows, are linked by eight walkways.
facts.quote: In the back of the complex, Bo Bardi included a pair of concrete towers which house sports facilities, perforated by globular windows and connected to each other by eight walkways.

facts.fact: Rough openings were knocked into the factory walls and fitted with bright red sliding screens.
facts.quote: Rough windows were knocked out of the factory walls and covered with bright red sliding screens attached inside.

facts.fact: It is a Brutalist building known for its architectural and social qualities.
facts.quote: SESC Pompeia is a brutalist building renowned by its architectural and social qualities.

facts.fact: Trellick Tower in Kensal Town, London, opened in 1972; the Greater London Council commissioned it and Ernő Goldfinger designed it in the Brutalist style.
facts.quote: Opened in 1972, it was commissioned by the Greater London Council and designed in the Brutalist style by architect Ernő Goldfinger.

facts.fact: It was planned as an improvement on Goldfinger's earlier Balfron Tower and was his last major project.
facts.quote: The tower was planned to replace outdated social accommodation, and designed as an improvement on Goldfinger's earlier Balfron Tower in Poplar, East London. It was the last major project he worked on, and featured various space-saving designs, along with a separate access tower containing a plant room.

facts.fact: The 31-floor tower has a separate lift and service tower linked to the access corridors every third storey.
facts.quote: It has a long, thin profile, with a separate lift and service tower linked at every third storey to the access corridors in the main building, which overall has 31 floors.

facts.fact: A projecting plant room at the top of the service tower held the main heating system.
facts.quote: The service tower has two additional floors higher than the main building, which includes a projecting plant room that holds the main heating system.

facts.fact: Space-saving details include sliding bathroom doors and light switches set into door surrounds.
facts.quote: He included a number of space-saving designs, such as using sliding doors to access bathrooms, and light switches embedded in the door surrounds.

facts.fact: Goldfinger said building high was meant to free the ground for people to enjoy.
facts.quote: Goldfinger said "the whole object of building high is to free the ground for children and grown-ups to enjoy Mother Earth and not to cover every inch with bricks and mortar".

facts.fact: A local landmark, it has been Grade II* listed since 1998, which has kept its distinctive concrete facade.
facts.quote: A local landmark, it has been Grade II* listed since 1998, and has retained its distinctive concrete facade as a result.

facts.fact: The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour, widely seen as a masterpiece of 20th-century architecture.
facts.quote: Located on the foreshore of Sydney Harbour, it is widely regarded as one of the world's most famous and distinctive buildings, and a masterpiece of 20th-century architecture.

facts.fact: Jørn Utzon won the 1957 design competition; an Australian team led by Peter Hall completed it, and it opened on 20 October 1973.
facts.quote: Designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon and completed by an Australian architectural team headed by Peter Hall, the building was formally opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 20 October 1973, 16 years after Utzon's 1957 selection as winner of an international design competition.

facts.fact: Its roofs are precast concrete 'shells', each a section of a sphere of 75.2 m radius, set on a monumental podium.
facts.quote: The facility features a modern expressionist design, with a series of large precast concrete "shells", each composed of sections of a sphere of 75.2 metres (246 ft 8.6 in) radius, forming the roofs of the structure, set on a monumental podium.

facts.fact: Making every shell part of one sphere, found in 1961, let arch segments be cast in a common mould.
facts.quote: In mid-1961, the design team found a solution to the problem: the shells all being created as sections from a sphere. This solution allows arches of varying length to be cast in a common mould, and a number of arch segments of common length to be placed adjacent to one another, to form a spherical section.

facts.fact: The shells look white but carry a chevron pattern of over a million glossy white and matte cream tiles.
facts.quote: Though the shells appear uniformly white from a distance, they actually feature a subtle chevron pattern composed of 1,056,006 tiles in two colours: glossy white and matte cream.

facts.fact: Utzon resigned in 1966 after the ministry in charge criticised the project's cost and time and judged his designs impractical.
facts.quote: Due to the Ministry's criticism of the project's costs and time, along with their impression of Utzon's designs being impractical, this ultimately led to his resignation in 1966 (see below).

facts.fact: It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, the Sydney Opera House became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, having been listed on the (now defunct) Register of the National Estate since 1980, the National Trust of Australia register since 1983, the City of Sydney Heritage Inventory since 2000, the New South Wales State Heritage Register since 2003, and the Australian National Heritage List since 2005.

facts.fact: The museum stands at Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, on the banks of the Sabarmati river.
facts.quote: It is located at Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, India on the banks of River Sabarmati.

facts.fact: Charles Correa designed it, starting in 1958.
facts.quote: It was designed by the renowned architect Charles Correa beginning in 1958.

facts.fact: It was Correa's first important commission: 51 modular units, each 6 × 6 m, around a water court.
facts.quote: The museum, Correa's first important commission, consisted originally of 51 modular units, each 6 x 6 metres, surrounding a water court.

facts.fact: Jawaharlal Nehru opened it in 1963.
facts.quote: The complex was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963.

facts.fact: It holds tens of thousands of letters to and by Gandhi, with photographs and books.
facts.quote: It houses tens of thousands of letters to and by Gandhi, as well as photographs and books.

facts.fact: The museum was first kept in Hridaya Kunj, Gandhi's own cottage in the ashram.
facts.quote: The ashram now has a museum, the Gandhi Smarak Sangrahalaya. This had originally been located in Hridaya Kunj, Gandhi's own cottage in the ashram.

facts.fact: Charles Correa's Kanchanjunga apartments in Mumbai are cited as a modern example of high-rise courtyards in India's tradition of climate-responsive building.
facts.quote: India has a history of bioclimatic architecture. From a courtyard Haveli in Rajasthan that stores the cool air from the night before to Charles Correa's contemporary examples of high-rise courtyards in the Kanchanjunga apartments, Mumbai

facts.fact: Geoffrey Bawa designed the Kandalama Hotel in Sri Lanka, built between 1992 and 1995.
facts.quote: The Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa designed the Kandalama Hotel which was built between 1992 and 1995.

facts.fact: The 152-room, six-storey hotel stands on the shore of the Kandalama Reservoir, 12 km from Dambulla.
facts.quote: The 152-room Heritance Kandalama is situated 12 kilometres (7.5 mi) from Dambulla on the shores of the Kandalama Reservoir. The hotel is six-storeyed.

facts.fact: Bawa planned the arrival so that the distant view of Sigiriya is revealed only after entering the lobby.
facts.quote: Bawa was interested in developing a spatial and visual sequence of entry that culminated in the revelation of the distant view of the monument of Sigiriya only after entry to the hotel lobby.

facts.fact: The hotel wraps around a cliff, with a large cave-like porte-cochère against its western side.
facts.quote: One of the hotel's dominant design features is the large, cave-like porte-cochère abutting the western side of the cliff around which the hotel wraps.

facts.fact: It was the first LEED-certified green building outside the United States and the first LEED-certified hotel in the world.
facts.quote: Kandalama is the first LEED-certified green building outside of the United States, as well as the first LEED-certified green hotel in the world.

facts.fact: It was the first hotel in Asia accredited to the Green Globe standard.
facts.quote: Heritance Kandalama became the first hotel in Asia to be accredited with the Green Globe standard.

facts.fact: Its construction was controversial, first over ecology and later over its effect on local culture.
facts.quote: The ecological concerns dominated the debate initially, however, the perceived negative impact of the local culture was cited as the reason for opposition later.

facts.fact: Hassan Fathy built New Qurna (New Gourna) between 1946 and 1952 on Luxor's West Bank to rehouse the people of Qurna.
facts.quote: New Qurna was built between 1946 and 1952 by Egyptian architect Hassan Fathy midway between the Colossi of Memnon and el-Gezira on the Nile on the main road to the Theban Necropolis to house the residents of the Qurna.

facts.fact: The aim was low-cost, environmentally friendly buildings.
facts.quote: New Qurna served to relocate the villagers, but it also served to be an experiment. The goal was to make the low cost buildings, as well as environment friendly structures.

facts.fact: Fathy's plan relied on appropriate technology, above all mud brick construction.
facts.quote: To address this issue, Fathy instead devised a plan that included the use of appropriate technology, notably mud brick construction.

facts.fact: He drew on Nubian building he saw in 1941: enclosed courtyards and vaulted roofs.
facts.quote: With regard to aesthetic issues, Fathy placed emphasis on traditional Nubian architectural designs which he observed in a 1941 trip to the region (enclosed courtyards; vaulted roofing), yielding what Fathy described as "spacious, lovely, clean, and harmonious houses."

facts.fact: The villagers were not keen to move, as it cut them off from their living trading in archaeological finds.
facts.quote: Despite this, inhabitants of the former village were not enthusiastic about relocating, which effectively cut them off from their existing livelihood of trading in archaeological finds.

facts.fact: The village was never finished; today only the mosque, market and a few houses of the original remain.
facts.quote: The design, which combined traditional materials and techniques with modern principles was never completed and much of the fabric of the village has since been lost; all what remains today of the original New Qurna is the mosque, market and a few houses.

facts.fact: New Qurna was put on the 2010 World Monuments Watch list because of its importance to town planning and vernacular architecture and the loss of much of its original form.
facts.quote: New Qurna was added to the 2010 World Monuments Watch List of Most Endangered Sites to bring attention to the site's importance to modern town planning and vernacular architecture due to the loss of much of the original form of the village since it was built.

facts.fact: Kolumba stands on the site of the old St. Kolumba church, destroyed in the Second World War, and takes in Gottfried Böhm's 1950 chapel 'Madonna of the Ruins'.
facts.quote: It is located at the historic site of the former St. Kolumba church, destroyed during World War II, and also includes the 1950 chapel "Madonna of the Ruins" by Gottfried Böhm.

facts.fact: Atelier Zumthor won the competition in 1997; the cornerstone was laid in 2003 and the museum was consecrated in September 2007.
facts.quote: Atelier Zumthor won the architectural competition in 1997. Planning lasted until 2003, with the cornerstone laid on 1 October 2003 and the building consecrated on 15 September 2007 by Cardinal Meisner.

facts.fact: Zumthor built on the original foundations and remains of St. Kolumba, joining old and new.
facts.quote: Zumthor implemented the juxtaposition of old and new by constructing on the original foundation and remains of St. Kolumba.

facts.fact: A perforated grey brick facade wraps like a cloak around the museum, the church ruins and the 1950s chapel.
facts.quote: The new structure Peter Zumthor built for the museum now shares its site with the ruins of the Gothic church and the 1950s chapel, wrapping a perforated grey brick facade like a cloak around both, the museum and old church.

facts.fact: The bricks were specially fired to match the stone and brick of the destroyed Romanesque church.
facts.quote: The visible brickwork, specially fired for this project, harmonizes with the natural stone and brick masonry of the Romanesque church destroyed in World War II and the post-war concrete blocks.

facts.fact: The galleries are lit by daylight, and artificial lighting is avoided.
facts.quote: The exhibition spaces are illuminated by natural daylight; artificial lighting is avoided.

facts.fact: The ground floor holds the excavation site, crossed by a walkway over the ancient foundations.
facts.quote: The ground floor houses the excavation site with a walkway across ancient foundations and includes the chapel as an integrated space.

facts.fact: It won the DAM Prize for Architecture in Germany in 2008.
facts.quote: 2008: DAM Prize for Architecture in Germany

facts.fact: The Row House in Sumiyoshi, also called Azuma House, is a home in Osaka designed by Tadao Ando early in his career.
facts.quote: Row House in Sumiyoshi (住吉の長屋, Sumiyoshi no Nagaya), also called Azuma House (Japanese 東邸), is a personal residence in Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka, Japan. It was designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando in his early career.

facts.fact: It is a small two-storey house of cast-in-place concrete, finished in 1976, where Ando's characteristic style began to show.
facts.quote: His Row House in Sumiyoshi (Azuma House, 住吉の長屋), a small two-story, cast-in-place concrete house completed in 1976, is an early work which began to show elements of his characteristic style.

facts.fact: It has no exterior windows; an inner courtyard makes up for the lost light.
facts.quote: It was designed without exterior windows reflecting the desire of the owner to feel that he was not "in Japan", but to compensate for lost light, an interior courtyard with cross walkway was created.

facts.fact: The house is three equal rectangular volumes: two enclosed rooms either side of an open courtyard.
facts.quote: It consists of three equal rectangular volumes: two enclosed volumes of interior spaces separated by an open courtyard.

facts.fact: The open courtyard brings light, air and weather inside and links the rooms on either side.
facts.quote: The open courtyard provides natural light, air, and exposure to the weather, while also connecting the living spaces on either side.

facts.fact: Upstairs, a bridge crosses the courtyard between the bedrooms.
facts.quote: On the second floor, a bridge connects the bedrooms across the courtyard.

facts.fact: Sendai Mediatheque, a library and art gallery in Sendai, was Toyo Ito's winning competition entry of 1995 and opened in January 2001.
facts.quote: Toyo Ito's winning entry for an open competition commissioned by the city of Sendai in 1995, the innovative building opened to the public in January 2001.

facts.fact: Its seven floor plates are held up by a 'forest' of 13 irregular tubes that seem to rise fluidly through the building.
facts.quote: The seven platforms are supported by what Ito calls "characterizing" architectural elements: a forest of 13 non-uniform tubes which appear to rise fluidly through the building.

facts.fact: The structure has three main parts: tubes, plates and skin.
facts.quote: The structure of the Sendai Mediatheque is composed of three main elements: tubes, plates and skin.

facts.fact: The floor plates are a honeycomb of steel sections filled with lightweight concrete, spanning between the tubes without beams.
facts.quote: The plates (floor slabs) are composed of a honeycomb-like network of steel sections infilled with lightweight concrete. The steel honeycomb structure allows the plate to span between irregularly spaced vertical supports without beams, and with minimal thickness of the slab itself.

facts.fact: The tubes look continuous but were made in floor-high pieces and assembled floor by floor.
facts.quote: Although they appear to be continuous, the tubes were actually manufactured in floor-height segments and were assembled sequentially, floor-by-floor.

facts.fact: The building survived the March 2011 earthquake with little or no damage.
facts.quote: As a test to its integrity, the building survived the March 2011 earthquake with little to no damage.

facts.fact: The double-glazed south facade is part of the building's climate control.
facts.quote: The main (south-facing) facade is double-glazed and functions as part of the building's climate control system.

facts.fact: Ito cited Mies's Barcelona Pavilion and Le Corbusier's Dom-ino house as precedents.
facts.quote: Ito also refers to Mies' Barcelona Pavilion and Le Corbusier’s Dom-ino house as precedents for his work, and indeed, the Mediatheque appears to mix concepts from the two projects, combining le Corbusier’s play with slab and column structure, with Mies “fluid” spatial effects achieved through combined transparency and reflectivity of materials.

facts.fact: The Teshima Art Museum holds a single artwork, on the island of Teshima in Japan's Seto Inland Sea.
facts.quote: The Teshima Art Museum (豊島美術館, Teshima Bijitsukan) hosts a single piece of artwork and is located on the island of Teshima, Kagawa Prefecture, Japan, in the Seto Inland Sea.

facts.fact: Its architect is Ryue Nishizawa, co-founder of SANAA.
facts.quote: The architect is Ryue Nishizawa (co-founder of SANAA).

facts.fact: The building is a freestanding concrete shell 25 cm thick, 40 by 60 m, and 4 m high at its highest point.
facts.quote: The museum building is made of a freestanding concrete shell which is 25 cm-thick, 40 by 60 meters, and 4 meters at its highest point.

facts.fact: The artwork inside, Matrix, is by the sculptor Rei Naito.
facts.quote: The artwork is titled Matrix and was created by sculptor Rei Naito.

facts.fact: The Lloyd's building, nicknamed the Inside-Out Building, is the home of the insurance market Lloyd's of London.
facts.quote: The Lloyd's building (sometimes known as the Inside-Out Building) is the home of the insurance institution Lloyd's of London.

facts.fact: It is a leading example of Bowellism: services such as ducts and lifts are on the outside to free the interior.
facts.quote: The building is a leading example of radical Bowellism architecture in which the services for the building, such as ducts and lifts, are located on the exterior to maximise space in the interior.

facts.fact: Richard Rogers & Partners designed it, and it was built between 1978 and 1986.
facts.quote: The current Lloyd's building (address 1 Lime Street) was designed by the architect company Richard Rogers & Partners and built between 1978 and 1986.

facts.fact: Its 12 glass lifts were the first of their kind in the UK, and the design owes much to Archigram.
facts.quote: The 12 glass lifts were the first of their kind in the United Kingdom. Like the Pompidou Centre, the building was highly influenced by the work of Archigram in the 1950s and 1960s.

facts.fact: Three main towers and three service towers stand around a central rectangular space.
facts.quote: The building consists of three main towers and three service towers around a central, rectangular space.

facts.fact: Galleries around the Underwriting Room form a 60 m atrium lit through a huge barrel-vaulted glass roof.
facts.quote: The Underwriting Room (often simply called "the Room") is overlooked by galleries, forming a 60 metres (197 ft) high atrium lit naturally through a huge barrel-vaulted glass roof.

facts.fact: In 2011 it was listed Grade I, the youngest building ever to receive that status.
facts.quote: In 2011, twenty-five years after its completion in 1986 the building received Grade I listing; at this time it was the youngest structure ever to obtain this status.

facts.fact: The exposed services have made maintenance very expensive.
facts.quote: Its innovation of having key service pipes and other components routed outside the walls has led to very expensive maintenance costs due to their exposure to the elements.

facts.fact: The HSBC Main Building in Hong Kong is a steel suspended structure designed by Norman Foster, completed in November 1985 and opened in April 1986.
facts.quote: The current building is a steel suspended structure designed by Norman Foster, was completed on 18 November 1985. The building officially opened on 7 April 1986.

facts.fact: When finished it was the most expensive building in the world.
facts.quote: At the time, it was the most expensive building in the world (c.a. HK$5.2 billion, roughly US$668 million).

facts.fact: It is 178.8 m high, with 47 storeys and four basement levels.
facts.quote: The building is 178.8 metres high with 47 storeys and four basement levels.

facts.fact: It is built of five steel modules prefabricated in the UK near Glasgow and shipped to Hong Kong.
facts.quote: The building has a modular design consisting of five steel modules, which were prefabricated in the UK by Scott Lithgow Shipbuilders near Glasgow and shipped to Hong Kong.

facts.fact: Eight groups of four aluminium-clad steel columns rise from the foundations, with five levels of triangular suspension trusses locked into these masts.
facts.quote: It consists of eight groups of four aluminium-clad steel columns which ascend from the foundations up through the core structure, and five levels of triangular suspension trusses which are locked into these masts.

facts.fact: Its circulation was planned to let people meet between floors, creating 'a village in the sky'.
facts.quote: The goal of this design is to add a social dimension and social flow to each floor, allowing for conversations to occur between floors and creating "a village in the sky".

facts.fact: A mirror system at the top of the atrium reflects sunlight into the building.
facts.quote: There is a mirror system at the top of the atrium, which reflects natural sunlight into the building.

facts.fact: Its cooling system uses seawater instead of fresh water.
facts.quote: The building’s cooling system relies on seawater rather than fresh water, a solution that minimizes environmental impact in the coastal city of Hong Kong.

facts.fact: Frank Gehry designed the building, which stands beside the Nervión river as it runs through Bilbao to the sea.
facts.quote: The building, designed by Canadian-American architect Frank Gehry, was built alongside the Nervion River, which runs through the city to the Cantabrian Sea.

facts.fact: Gehry said the seemingly random curves of the exterior are designed to catch the light.
facts.quote: The curves on the exterior of the building were intended to appear random; the architect said that "the randomness of the curves are designed to catch the light".

facts.fact: The interior is organised around a large, light-filled atrium that Gehry nicknamed The Flower.
facts.quote: The atrium, which Gehry nicknamed The Flower because of its shape, serves as the organizing center of the museum.

facts.fact: Ten of the nineteen galleries are orthogonal and clad in stone; the other nine are irregular and clad in titanium.
facts.quote: The 11,000 m2 (120,000 sq ft) of exhibition space are distributed over nineteen galleries, ten of which follow a classic orthogonal plan that can be identified from the exterior by their stone finishes. The remaining nine galleries are irregularly shaped and can be identified from the outside by their swirling organic forms and titanium cladding.

facts.fact: The outer skin is made of 33,000 titanium plates.
facts.quote: The museum's exterior skin is made of 33,000 titanium plates, a material that has been used to replace copper or lead because of their toxicity.

facts.fact: To control costs, Gehry used computer models made with CATIA software and worked closely with each building trade.
facts.quote: Third, he used computer visualizations produced by Rick Smith employing Dassault Systemes' CATIA V3 software and collaborated closely with the individual building trades to control costs during construction.

facts.fact: Its effect on the city became known as the 'Bilbao effect'.
facts.quote: The museum was opened as part of a revitalization effort for the city of Bilbao, and its impact on the city quarter became known as the Bilbao effect.

facts.fact: Experts in the 2010 World Architecture Survey named it more often than any other building as one of the most important works since 1980.
facts.quote: The museum was the building most frequently named as one of the most important works completed since 1980 in the 2010 World Architecture Survey among architecture experts.

facts.fact: Tate Modern, opened in 2000, is Herzog & de Meuron's conversion of London's disused Bankside Power Station into a gallery of modern art.
facts.quote: Tate Modern in London, which transformed a disused power station into a modern art gallery. Opened in 2000, the Tate Modern has become one of the most visited art museums in the world, celebrated for its innovative design that seamlessly blends industrial elements with contemporary art spaces.

facts.fact: The conversion blended industrial history with contemporary design.
facts.quote: The transformation of London's Bankside Power Station into the Tate Modern (2000) marked a turning point, blending industrial history with contemporary design.

facts.fact: The New York Times praised it as an example of how architecture can breathe new life into old structures.
facts.quote: The New York Times praised it as "an example of how architecture can breathe new life into old structures."

facts.fact: The project gave Herzog & de Meuron their international reputation.
facts.quote: Their work on the conversion of the Bankside Power Station into the Tate Modern in London (2000) gained them an international reputation as architects.

facts.fact: The Jewish Museum Berlin opened in 2001 and is the largest Jewish museum in Europe.
facts.quote: The Jewish Museum Berlin (Jüdisches Museum Berlin) was opened in 2001 and is the largest Jewish museum in Europe.

facts.fact: Where other entrants proposed neutral spaces, Daniel Libeskind offered a radical zigzag, nicknamed 'Blitz' (lightning).
facts.quote: While other entrants proposed cool, neutral spaces, Libeskind offered a radical, zigzag design, which earned the nickname "Blitz" ("Lightning").

facts.fact: The Libeskind building, about 15,000 m², is a twisted zigzag reached only by an underground passage from the old building.
facts.quote: The Libeskind building, consisting of about 15,000 m2 (160,000 sq ft), is a twisted zig-zag and is accessible only via an underground passage from the old building.

facts.fact: A line of empty 'Voids', about 20 m tall, cuts straight through the whole building.
facts.quote: A line of "Voids", empty spaces about 66 feet (20 m) tall, slices linearly through the entire building.

facts.fact: Three slanting underground 'Axes' stand for continuity in German history, emigration and the Holocaust.
facts.quote: In Berlin, the three axes symbolize three paths of Jewish life in Germany – continuity in German history, emigration from Germany, and the Holocaust.

facts.fact: The Garden of Exile has a tilted base, with oleaster growing out of reach on 49 tall pillars.
facts.quote: The second axis connects the Museum proper to the Garden of Exile, whose foundation is tilted. The Garden's oleaster grows out of reach, atop 49 tall pillars (48 filled with Berlin's earth, one with earth from Jerusalem).

facts.fact: The bare concrete Holocaust Tower is neither heated nor cooled and is lit only by a small slit in its roof.
facts.quote: The bare concrete Tower is neither heated nor cooled, and its only light comes from a small slit in its roof.

facts.fact: Empty when finished in 1999, the building drew over 350,000 visitors before the exhibits went in.
facts.quote: The empty museum was completed in 1999 and attracted over 350,000 people before it was filled and opened on 9 September 2001.

facts.fact: The Oslo Opera House is the home of the Norwegian National Opera and Ballet, in Bjørvika at the head of the Oslofjord.
facts.quote: The Oslo Opera House (Norwegian: Operahuset) is the home of the Norwegian National Opera and Ballet, and the national opera house in Norway. The building is situated in the Bjørvika neighbourhood of central Oslo, at the head of the Oslofjord.

facts.fact: Snøhetta's design was chosen from 350 competition entries.
facts.quote: A design competition was held and, of the 350 entries received, the judges chose that of the Norwegian architectural firm Snøhetta.

facts.fact: Built from 2003 to 2007, it was finished ahead of schedule and under budget.
facts.quote: Construction started in 2003 and was completed in 2007, ahead of schedule and 300 million NOK (~US$52 million) under its budget of 4.4 billion NOK (~US$760 million).

facts.fact: Its angled outer surfaces, clad in Carrara marble and white granite, make it seem to rise from the water.
facts.quote: The angled exterior surfaces of the building are covered with marble from Carrara, Italy and white granite and make it appear to rise from the water.

facts.fact: The roof slopes down to ground level, forming a large plaza where people can walk up for views over Oslo.
facts.quote: The roof of the building angles to ground level, creating a large plaza that invites pedestrians to walk up and enjoy the panoramic views of Oslo.

facts.fact: The lobby has 15 m tall windows with minimal frames, and thin angled columns hold the roof without blocking views.
facts.quote: The lobby is surrounded by 15 m (49 ft) tall windows with minimal framing and special glass that allows maximum views of the water. The roof is supported by thin angled columns also designed not to interfere with views.

facts.fact: Oak lines the interiors, a warm contrast to the cool white outside.
facts.quote: Interior surfaces are covered in oak to bring warmth to spaces in contrast to the coolness of the white exterior.

facts.fact: It won the 2009 European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture.
facts.quote: The Opera House won the culture award at the World Architecture Festival in Barcelona in October 2008 and the 2009 European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture.

facts.fact: The Elbphilharmonie is a concert hall in Hamburg's HafenCity, on the Elbe river.
facts.quote: The Elbphilharmonie (German pronunciation: [ˈɛlpfɪlhaʁmoˌniː] ; "Elbe Philharmonic Hall"), popularly nicknamed Elphi, is a concert hall in the HafenCity quarter of Hamburg, Germany, on the Grasbrook peninsula of the Elbe River.

facts.fact: A new glass structure, like a sail, wave or crystal, sits on top of an old brick warehouse, Kaispeicher A.
facts.quote: The new construction resembles a hoisted sail, water wave, iceberg or quartz crystal resting on top of an old brick warehouse (Kaispeicher A, built in 1963) near the historical Speicherstadt.

facts.fact: The glassy superstructure has its own foundation and a wavy roofline; about a thousand of its windows are curved.
facts.quote: On top of this a footprint-matching superstructure rests on its own foundation exhibiting a glassy exterior and a wavy roof line. About one thousand glass windows are curved.

facts.fact: At 108 m it is the tallest inhabited building in Hamburg.
facts.quote: It is the key project of the new Hafencity development and the tallest inhabited building in Hamburg, with a final height of 108 metres (354 ft).

facts.fact: A curved escalator leads to the Plaza, a viewing deck on the 8th floor at the top of the brick base.
facts.quote: A curved escalator from the main entrance at the east side connects the ground floor with an observation deck, the Plaza, at the 8th floor, the top of the brick section.

facts.fact: The 2,100-seat Great Concert Hall is in vineyard style, with the performers in the middle and the audience all around.
facts.quote: The Great Concert Hall can accommodate 2,100 visitors whereby the performers are in the center of the hall surrounded by the audience in the vineyard style arrangement.

facts.fact: Yasuhisa Toyota designed the acoustics, using about 10,000 individually shaped plates to disperse sound.
facts.quote: The acoustics were designed by Yasuhisa Toyota who installed about 10,000 individually microshaped drywall plates to disperse sound waves.

facts.fact: It was criticised for cost and schedule overruns: about €200 million estimated, €870 million final.
facts.quote: The project was criticized because of its cost and schedule overruns; construction was originally estimated to cost about €200 million, while the final cost was €870 million.

facts.fact: The Louvre Abu Dhabi is an art museum on Saadiyat Island, run under a 2007 agreement between the UAE and France.
facts.quote: The Louvre Abu Dhabi (Arabic: اللوفر أبوظبي, romanized: al-lūfr ʔabū ẓaby; French: Louvre Abou Dabi) is an art museum located on Saadiyat Island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It runs under an agreement between the UAE and France, signed in March 2007, that allows it to use the Louvre's name until 2047, and has been described by the Louvre as "France's largest cultural project abroad."

facts.fact: Abu Dhabi chose Jean Nouvel, architect of the Arab World Institute in Paris, in 2006.
facts.quote: Meanwhile, the Abu Dhabi authorities in 2006 selected Jean Nouvel, known among other projects for having designed the Arab World Institute in Paris, as the building's architect.

facts.fact: Nouvel designed a seemingly floating dome whose web pattern lets the sun filter through.
facts.quote: During the initial Concept Design phase in 2006–2007, Jean Nouvel and his team designed the museum as a "seemingly floating dome structure"; its web-patterned dome allowing the sun to filter through.

facts.fact: The effect is meant to recall sunlight passing through date palm fronds in an oasis.
facts.quote: The overall effect is meant to represent "rays of sunlight passing through date palm fronds in an oasis."

facts.fact: The dome is made of 7,850 aluminium stars in eight layers, forming a perforated roof that lets sunlight through.
facts.quote: Their structural engineers realised the "floating dome" from 7,850 aluminium stars of varying sizes, which tessellate over eight layers to create a perforated roof structure that allows sunlight through to the spaces below.

facts.fact: Tidal pools among the galleries give the feel of a 'museum in the sea', with a watertight basement against the marine setting.
facts.quote: A team of specialist geotechnical and water engineers designed a watertight basement and tidal pools within the galleries to give the illusion of a "museum in the sea" while protecting artwork, artefacts and visitors from the corrosive marine environment.

facts.fact: Under the dome are 55 buildings, 23 of them galleries, shaped like the region's low-rise homes.
facts.quote: Guests who visit the museum can discover the 55 buildings of which 23 are art galleries and are constructed to look like the low-rise home of the region.

facts.fact: It opened on 8 November 2017.
facts.quote: The museum was eventually inaugurated on 8 November 2017 by French President Emmanuel Macron, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince (and de facto ruler) Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and UAE Prime Minister and Emir of Dubai Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

facts.fact: Metropol Parasol, known as Las Setas ('The Mushrooms'), was launched in 2004 to revive the Plaza de la Encarnación in Seville, long used as a car park.
facts.quote: In 2004 the Metropol Parasol project, commonly known as Las Setas ('The Mushrooms'), due to the appearance of the structure, was launched to revitalise the Plaza de la Encarnación, for years used as a car park and seen as a dead spot between more popular tourist destinations in the city.

facts.fact: It was finished in March 2011 at just over €102 million, more than twice the planned cost.
facts.quote: The Metropol Parasol was completed in March 2011, costing just over €102 million in total, more than twice as much as originally planned.

facts.fact: Built of crossed wooden beams, it is said to be the largest timber-framed structure in the world.
facts.quote: Constructed from crossed wooden beams, Las Setas is said to be the largest timber-framed structure in the world.

facts.fact: Roman remains are displayed in place in its underground Antiquarium.
facts.quote: Existing Roman features in Seville itself include the remains exposed in situ in the underground Antiquarium of the Metropol Parasol building, the remnants of an aqueduct, three pillars of a temple in Mármoles Street, the columns of La Alameda de Hércules and the remains in the Patio de Banderas square near the Seville Cathedral.

facts.fact: Jürgen Mayer's project for the plaza ran from 2004 to 2011.
facts.quote: Metropol Parasol, redevelopment of the Plaza de la Encarnacion, Seville, Spain, 2004–2011

facts.fact: It was a finalist for the 2013 European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture.
facts.quote: Finalist European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture, 2013 for Metropol Parasol

facts.fact: The Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, by Zaha Hadid, is a 57,500 m² complex known for its flowing curves and lack of sharp angles.
facts.quote: The Heydar Aliyev Center (Azerbaijani: Heydər Əliyev Mərkəzi) is a 57,500 m2 (619,000 sq ft) building complex in Baku, Azerbaijan, designed by Zaha Hadid and noted for its distinctive architecture and flowing, curved style that eschews sharp angles.

facts.fact: Hadid was appointed after a competition in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, Zaha Hadid was appointed as the design architect of the Center after a competition.

facts.fact: Its fluid form comes from folding the landscape's natural topography and wrapping the building's separate functions.
facts.quote: The Heydar Aliyev Center represents a fluid form which emerges by the folding of the landscape's natural topography and by the wrapping of individual functions of the Center.

facts.fact: All its functions and entrances are folds in a single continuous surface.
facts.quote: All functions of the Center, together with entrances, are represented by folds in a single continuous surface.

facts.fact: Over eight floor levels it holds a 1,000-seat auditorium, exhibition spaces, a conference centre, workshops and a museum.
facts.quote: Extending on eight floor levels, the center accommodates a 1,000-seat auditorium, temporary exhibition spaces, a conference center, workshops, and a museum.

facts.fact: It had its official soft opening on 10 May 2012.
facts.quote: The Heydar Aliyev Center had an official soft-opening ceremony on 10 May 2012 held by the president of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev.

facts.fact: In 2014 it won the Design Museum's Design of the Year, making Hadid the first woman to win, despite concerns over human rights.
facts.quote: In 2014, the Center won the Design Museum's Design of the Year Award 2014 despite concerns about the site's human rights record. This makes Hadid the first woman to win in that competition.

facts.fact: The High Line in New York is an urban landscape design by Diller Scofidio + Renfro.
facts.quote: The studio's international body of work includes notable examples of urban landscape design, such as the High Line in New York and Zaryadye Park in Moscow; institutional buildings, including museums such as The Broad and the United States Olympic & Paralympic Museum; and various installations, exhibitions, and performance projects.

facts.fact: DS+R made it with James Corner between 2009 and 2019.
facts.quote: High Line, New York, NY, (with James Corner; 2009–2019)

facts.fact: It was a collaboration with James Corner and Piet Oudolf and has been one of New York's signature destinations since it opened in 2009.
facts.quote: Among Scofidio's most well-known projects was the High Line, a collaboration with architects James Corner and Piet Oudolf. It has become one of New York's signature destinations since its opening in 2009.
